Primary audited checklist coverage, a conservative evidence-verified lower bound: **30/933 = 3.22%**. Each atomic mandatory hosting outcome has one binary point. Only `verified` earns a point. This measures evidence-complete coverage of this versioned checklist. It does not measure engineering effort, elapsed time, implementation completion, or an intrinsic percentage of Coolify.

Implementation presence is separate: 66 implemented, 283 partial, 584 missing. Verified: 30. These totals cannot be added.

Definition inventory: 934; eligible hosting outcomes: 933. Deferred Task-derived preview R54-C03 is retained outside this numerator, denominator and hosting-gate boundary.

Original inventory: 68 requirement parents, 37 acceptance parents, and 58 matrix parents: 19 areas, 9 databases, 10 sources, 3 secret providers, 7 builders, 4 proxies, and 6 notification channels. Parent/gate rows receive no extra score.

Fully complete requirement parents: 0/68. Acceptance gates passed: 0/37. Matrix gates passed: 0/58.

Full parity is not accepted until all applicable requirement, acceptance and matrix release gates pass. A future 100% atomic score alone does not establish release acceptance.

## Method and scope

Each criterion is a mandatory hosting outcome. Matrix breadth is expanded under its owning requirement and scores once. Acceptance scenarios and all matrix parents are binary release gates with zero extra weight.
Criteria were reviewed against the complete original R01-R68 text and the surrounding compatibility-ledger obligations. Full source rows and clause-review records remain in JSON. Compound runtime outcomes require the whole declared result, not a count of files, functions, commits or passing assertions.
Implementation presence records missing, partial or implemented. Evidence state records missing, partial, implemented, verified, evidence_unavailable or failed. Only verified contributes 1. Every other state contributes 0. A fully complete R requires all child criteria and applicable acceptance/matrix gates to pass.
R44 database rows duplicate the specification engine table and are cross-linked. The specification product-area table duplicates the ledger area inventory. Neither creates additional parent rows or points. Architecture/version, engine lifecycle, Compose raw/differential behavior, notification safety and extended infrastructure obligations are retained even when they are prose outside tables.
The denominator is a reviewed decomposition, not a mechanically discovered feature count. Source/inventory/hash checks establish integrity; independent specification review must assess whether all clauses are represented without duplicate outcomes.
Eligible hosting criteria alone define the primary denominator. Deferred Task-derived preview remains in the definition inventory with explicit deferred_task eligibility and zero current hosting weight. A hosting gate evaluates only eligible criteria; later Task claims need their own acceptance.
Parent criterion links and required gate dependencies are frozen with their own baseline digest. Passing a gate requires every eligible linked criterion and dependency gate plus a valid named combined acceptance receipt. A36 additionally requires all other A/matrix gates on the audited candidate.

Broad R08 Git/branch/commit choices cross-link the corresponding R09 source children; R44 engine rows specialize shared engine obligations and duplicate source tables add no score. Generic strategy outcomes and their specialized matrix outcomes were linked instead of scored twice where identified.
Original requirement sentences remain review units. The code validator checks their exact text and nonempty criterion links, but cannot prove human-language completeness or semantic nonduplication. Independent specification review is required before accepting this baseline.
Support-matrix criterion labels are proposed mandatory acceptance boundaries, not passing tests. A criterion containing a bounded compound outcome passes only when all named parts pass; one assertion never supplies fractional credit.
Pre-acceptance repair removed broad event-selection/retry/deduplication/history points in favor of six channel specializations. Source-choice, provider-credential, frozen-manifest, build-placement, builder-credential/retention and external-secret policy aggregates were similarly replaced by existing child links. The JSON preacceptance_repairs list records every replacement; surviving criterion IDs remain stable.
Second pre-acceptance review scores deployment-trigger auth/identity/deduplication/revision/ordering contracts once across every declared provider and signed manual webhook. Provider realizations add only unscored gate acceptance. Analogue review also replaces generic resource rollback, engine action/rotation and secret delivery aggregates with existing boundary links; the dedup_family_review records the distinct boundaries intentionally retained.
Additional source/build spot-check removed repeated selected-digest, immutable-Git-receipt and effective-settings aggregates. Per-strategy cross-host delivery labels no longer include the separately scored platform/pull preflight; actual transport, current deployment admission and transfer-integrity enforcement remain distinct boundaries.

Scope exclusions and imported safety obligations:

- R69-R102 and A38-A66 are excluded from the primary hosting denominator. R07 imports the minimum R81/R82 untrusted-hosting isolation prerequisite. R13/R15 import the R87-R92 hosting input, trust, reuse and evidence-safety clauses. R17 imports R85 human production authorization for agent-produced work. These references do not make full workspace functionality a prerequisite for trusted hosting.
- R65 durable Task collaboration, goals/activity/workspace/checkpoint/checks/candidate/preview/budget/history UI is deferred. Direct navigation and hosting without a Task remain scored. R54 task-derived previews are conditional on a future Task implementation and are retained outside eligible hosting coverage.
- R68/A36 agreement of schema, API, permissions, audit, UI, operational behavior and tests is an aggregate release gate. It earns no extra feature point. Published support profiles and measured limits remain independently scored outcomes.
- Coolify client adapters are conditional release contracts. No endpoint/request/response/error/version inventory is declared, so their unresolved contract gate stays missing and outside the fixed hosting-feature denominator. No endpoint is invented and no empty inventory passes.
- Native Go agent instead of upstream SSH-only management is an explicit implementation difference. Test-CA HTTPS does not establish production DNS/ACME. Linux arm64 qualification does not establish amd64 or a full architecture/version matrix. Trusted Docker does not establish hostile-workload isolation.

A missing verification artifact or affected/unknown historical dependency removes verified credit. A source test is implementation evidence until its actual pass is retained. `partial` has zero points. No runtime tests are implied by generating this report.

Every source link points to an immutable excerpt appendix in this report, generated with `git show SHA:path`. Anchors include the full subject SHA, path hash and line range. Historical evidence has distinct targets even when its path and lines match the current source. No unpublished commit depends on a remote GitHub link. Read acceptance and matrix gates alongside the atomic checklist before making a release claim.

## Reproduce

Run from the repository root with Python 3 and Git. No network or third-party packages are required.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --write
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --check
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --self-test
```

`--check` validates the original inventory at the audited SHA, frozen criterion manifest, links, source ranges, evidence subjects and embedded pass artifacts, then rejects a stale generated report. `--self-test` exercises rejected missing/duplicate scope, invalid evidence and stale-report cases. Observed named-test output is preserved in the checklist, including current physical output converted with test2json. Historical receipts retain credit only after complete declared dependency equality. Generating this audit does not run application/runtime tests.

## Conditional client compatibility gate

Unresolved conditional Coolify client contract: select exact endpoints, versions, request/response/error behavior, authorization and lifecycle outcomes before implementing or claiming an adapter. No endpoint inventory is declared. Contract selection and its tests remain a required gate for any future client-compatibility claim; zero selected endpoints is not a pass.

Schema 1; scoring `hosting-atomic-v1`. Criterion IDs and outcome definitions are frozen for this baseline. A future scope revision must record added and removed IDs and publish both the old and new denominator. Changing evidence does not change the denominator.

## Update the audit

1. For evidence-only refresh, choose an exact clean candidate and update audit_sha plus scripts/parity_audit.py BASE together. Re-extract original source ranges/text at that candidate and compare changes. Preserve criterion IDs, outcome definitions and denominator. Update source-manifest hash constants if source ranges move, while preserving outcome definitions; any semantic scope change follows the separate scoring-version procedure.
2. Recheck each credited test subject and complete relevant source/test/config/tool/dependency inputs. Retain unchanged historical credit only with explicit relevance; affected or unknown evidence becomes unverified until rerun. Update embedded pass artifacts, exact tests, profile and limits.
3. For a true scope change, increment scoring_version and schema/history handling, record every added/removed criterion ID with reason, and publish old/new denominator. Update the calculator frozen inventory/manifest rules through review. Never silently reweight outcomes.
4. Regenerate the report with --write, run --check and --self-test, review specification and code hygiene at the same candidate, and commit the audit. No latest-main inference or automatic credit from passing-test counts is allowed.

```text
R02. Team and project authorization. Reuse existing identity and service-account behavior. Add explicit team ownership and server-access rules. Preserve current project permissions during migration. A viewer MUST not gain deploy, terminal, secret-reveal or data-deletion rights through a new UI or API.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l395-l395"></a>

```text
R03. Machine onboarding. Support local installation, manual agent enrollment and SSH-assisted remote enrollment where the host adapter supports them. Probe operating system, architecture, virtualization/runtime availability, disk capacity, connectivity and relevant ingress readiness. Display qualified roles and unmet prerequisites. Validate SSH host identity and include installations or service restarts in the reviewed onboarding operation. Do not advertise VM isolation based only on a CPU flag or machine label.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l397-l397"></a>

```text
R04. Credential separation. Bootstrap SSH credentials, enrolled-agent credentials, Git credentials and registry credentials MUST have separate scopes and lifecycles. State whether bootstrap credentials are retained for recovery. The browser MUST not receive permanent agent or host credentials.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l399-l399"></a>

```text
R05. Stable destinations. Machine and destination identity MUST survive agent process replacement. Every deploy, rollback, volume operation, backup, route change and scheduled command MUST identify its intended runtime boundary and data location. Matching tags do not authorize relocation. Preserve legacy Server identifiers through migration mappings.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l401-l401"></a>

```text
R06. Machine roles and lifecycle. Support declared build, agent, test, application, storage, ingress and model roles where qualified, including combined roles with bounded allocations. Provide drain, reconnect, credential rotation, maintenance and removal. Removal MUST not implicitly destroy workloads or data. Old agents MUST not claim unsupported operations. Show the impact of a role or availability change on persistent workloads and queued tasks.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l403-l403"></a>

```text
R07. Execution trust. Untrusted agent tasks and untrusted build inputs MUST use a qualified isolation profile under R81 and R82. A shared host Docker daemon remains an explicitly trusted deployment mode. Database-level team separation does not sandbox hostile workloads. A machine administrator remains trusted with guest data and secrets placed on that machine. Capability matching never grants access to a machine, dataset or private network.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l407-l407"></a>

```text
R08. Source choices. Support public/private Git, selected branches and commits, registry image tags or digests, stored Dockerfiles, Git Compose, pasted Compose and catalog templates. Preserve the source of truth for each. A no-Git input MUST not require a repository placeholder.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l409-l409"></a>

```text
R09. Git integrations. Provide repository and branch selection, scoped credentials, connection tests and webhook setup. Implement GitHub first, then the provider matrix in section 2. Generic Git and signed manual deploy webhooks remain supported paths.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l411-l411"></a>

```text
R10. Trigger integrity. Authenticate provider events, record delivery identity, deduplicate retries and bind a deployment to the intended source revision. Define how superseded queued changes are handled. A delayed older event MUST not silently replace a newer active release. Replaying a webhook MUST not create unbounded duplicate builds.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l413-l413"></a>

```text
R11. Build strategies. Support Dockerfile contexts and targets, automatic builders, static file packaging, compiled static output and Compose build sections. Record the exact builder/version and effective settings. Validate monorepo base paths, output directories and command overrides. Nixpacks and Railpack support must be tracked separately. Coolify currently marks Railpack as Beta. C12
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l415-l415"></a>

```text
R12. Static sites. Distinguish serving already-built files from compiling frontend source. Support publish directory, SPA fallback and configurable static-server behavior. A configuration baked into an image requires a rebuild rather than a misleading restart action. C13
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l417-l417"></a>

```text
R13. Build records and outputs. Record resolved source or workspace checkpoint, frozen build input manifest, platform, builder identity, logs, cache outcome and immutable output identities. Accept image tags as convenient inputs and record selected digests. Keep original build provenance when an artifact is reused. A deployment retry MUST not silently rebuild different contents. R87–R92 define input, trust and verification rules.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l419-l419"></a>

Subject `09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea`. Reproduce with `git show 09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea:docs/product-spec.md` and select lines 419-419.

```text
R14. Placement and image delivery. Support documented local builds and dedicated build workers. Remote builds MUST publish to an authorized registry or another qualified transfer mechanism. Verify target platform, artifact availability and pull access before mutation. A local image on one daemon is not available elsewhere by implication. The supervising build session MUST be owned by a remote service or worker so a submitting laptop disconnect does not cancel accepted work. Buildx provides a remote BuildKit driver, but product supervision and authorization remain NeroCD responsibilities. W12
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l421-l421"></a>

Subject `09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea`. Reproduce with `git show 09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea:docs/product-spec.md` and select lines 421-421.

```text
R15. Cache and retention. Expose layer-cache reuse, complete-artifact reuse and verification reuse as separate outcomes. Scope cache access by project/team and trust policy. Track output-affecting secret versions and dependency refresh rules. Provide independent controls for disabling cache, rebuilding an artifact, refreshing mutable inputs and rerunning checks. Protect artifacts referenced by active deployments, retained releases and evidence roots. R87–R92 define the detailed contract.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l423-l423"></a>

```text
R16. Build credentials and limits. Separate build-time credentials from runtime secrets. Scope source and registry access to the operation. Apply time, CPU, memory, disk and concurrency limits. A failed or canceled build MUST not modify the active resource or route. Untrusted preview code MUST not receive production credentials.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l429-l429"></a>

```text
R17. Automatic and protected deployments. Trusted push-triggered deployment remains a normal hosting workflow under an explicit resource/environment policy. Every deployment resolves a concrete release and target plan. Task work produced through an agent MUST pass independent human production authorization under R85. Agent access to a repository, branch or workflow MUST NOT become an indirect bypass of this rule through automatic deployment. New agent-workspace projects default production targets to protected.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l431-l431"></a>

### `docs/product-spec.md` lines 431-431

Subject `09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea`. Reproduce with `git show 09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea:docs/product-spec.md` and select lines 431-431.

```text
R18. Frozen release and plan identity. A release MUST identify immutable artifacts, source/build evidence and the deployable recipe version. A deployment plan freezes the selected release, destination, effective workload configuration, secret references/versions, relevant variable generations, required verification and data preconditions. Durable records MUST retain secret references and version identifiers instead of expanded values. Resolve secrets only into protected execution material. Secret-expanded Compose output MUST NOT enter ordinary release exports, audit payloads or artifacts. Hash normalized configuration with secret identities rather than publishing hashes derived from low-entropy values. Distinguish immutable secret-provider versions from mutable references.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l433-l433"></a>

### `docs/product-spec.md` lines 433-433

Subject `09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea`. Reproduce with `git show 09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea:docs/product-spec.md` and select lines 433-433.

```text
R19. Plan approval. Where approval is required, review the concrete plan after image preparation and required verification, before workload mutation. Bind the decision to release, target, effective configuration/secret generations and evidence. New selected contents, material evidence-policy changes, expiry or relevant plan changes require a new decision. Current authorization and revocation still apply at execution. State human self-approval policy separately from the prohibition on an agent approving its own production work.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l435-l435"></a>

Subject `09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea`. Reproduce with `git show 09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea:docs/product-spec.md` and select lines 435-435.

```text
R20. Admission and concurrency. Preserve durable idempotency and linked attempts. Scope active deployment exclusion to the resource binding. Extend current revision-level intent matching to release and plan identity. Coordinate shared proxy, network and storage mutations with their own ownership constraints.
```

Track raw Compose as an explicit parity mode that preserves operator-owned labels and networking and identifies which managed features are disabled. Raw mode MUST preserve authorization, destination ownership and data-retention rules. State its resolution and reproducibility limits for external inputs. Reject a protected-deployment policy during preflight if the raw definition cannot satisfy its required release guarantees without alteration.

Record resource identity, engine/version, size, digest and available locations. Use local staging and S3-compatible remote storage where configured. A storage backup MUST state whether writers remain active or are quiesced. For a stop-during-backup policy, record which containers were running, stop the required writers, create the archive, and attempt to resume those containers after success, failure or timeout. Do not start containers that were already stopped. Reconcile incomplete resume attempts and preserve their failure evidence. A live file archive MUST NOT be labeled an application-consistent database backup.

```text
R47. Partial outcomes and retention. Distinguish dump/archive success from remote-upload success. Preserve the local recovery artifact after failed upload. Keep local and remote retention independent. Replaying a retention request after response loss must return its receipt without deleting another batch. Preserve audit and receipt atomicity.
```

In-place restore must identify its target, replacement behavior, compatibility, writer coordination and recovery point. Restore ownership and permissions where relevant. Verify an application can read and write restored data before marking the recovery test passed.

```text
R49. Platform recovery. Preserve the existing compatible-image/schema restore discipline and invalidation of restored sessions and active leases. Recover required secret keys and configuration. Enter a recovery mode that observes existing hosts and confirms ownership before resuming mutation. Do not recreate or delete healthy workloads merely because the control-plane database was restored.
```

```text
R50. Versioned templates. Store template identifier, source version, original definition, user changes, generated values, component identities and resolved images. Generate passwords and stable identifiers once. Redeployment and catalog refresh MUST not regenerate credentials.

Show a change preview for images, variables, mounts, networks, health and migrations. Catalog updates MUST not silently rewrite installed resources. Block or explain rollback when data compatibility prevents it.
```

Support single-image and declared Compose paths, including application, workers and isolated databases. Its lifecycle MUST be independent of the agent run and mutable workspace. Record the current immutable release and its verification coverage.

```text
R55. Preview trust and credentials. Default automatic previews to trusted repository actors and authenticated viewers. Public-fork execution requires an explicit policy and qualified isolation. Production secrets, database bindings and writable volumes MUST NOT be copied by default. Use isolated seed data unless a separate data-copy operation is authorized. Preview access, source editing and deployment permissions are distinct. Limits account for build and runtime capacity.
```

```text
R56. Preview lifecycle. Update a preview from its intended candidate, report provider/task status and URL, and expire it under a recorded policy. Define failed-update, retry, data retention and extension behavior. Ending an agent run MUST NOT remove a retained preview. A delayed close event or repeated cleanup MUST NOT delete production, external data or a newer unrelated preview. Closing the creator's client does not alter the preview lifetime.
```

```text
R57. Delivery policy. Expose auto-deploy branch selection, path filters where supported, manual deploy, deploy webhooks, optional approval and rollback policy. Keep ordinary push deployment simple. Advanced operational templates must not become mandatory configuration for a normal application.
```

```text
R58. Continuous observation. Collect server reachability, container state, readiness, disk usage and bounded CPU/memory samples independently of deployment jobs. Combine event-driven updates with periodic reconciliation. Document collection and stale-state thresholds. An unreachable agent means current state is unknown, not that every workload stopped.

Live follow must reconnect and indicate gaps or truncation. Keep audit records separate. External log drains and metrics export are part of the operations plan.
```

Display desired state, last operation result and latest observed state separately. Expose diagnostics and resource limits without requiring generic run IDs as the primary navigation.

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l559-l559"></a>

Support server-level disablement, revocation and session termination. Audit session metadata without placing permanent credentials in the browser.

Record occurrence identity, schedule version and actual target. Define timezone, DST, timeout, overlap and missed-run policy. The default should skip missed runs and forbid overlap rather than create an uncontrolled catch-up burst.

Include deployments, backup/upload failures, schedules, resource state, server reachability and disk pressure. Persist delivery attempts, bounded retries and deduplication keys. Test delivery must be distinct from exercising an actual event.

```text
R64. Maintenance. Provide owned-image/cache cleanup, disk-pressure reporting, agent/proxy version visibility and supported upgrade procedures. Never prune all host resources indiscriminately. The main collaboration view is a durable Task showing its goal, source changes, agent/human activity, workspace status, checkpoint, required checks, candidate, preview, budget and deployment history. Provide direct navigation to projects, environments, applications, databases/stacks, machines, sources and settings. Users can host or operate an application without an agent task. Existing generic runs remain execution details and advanced automation, not a substitute for the new Task.
```

```text
R66. Complete UI workflows. After documented platform installation, every supported resource can be created and operated without seeded fixtures, SQL or ad hoc API calls. Preserve non-secret form input after validation failure. Show missing prerequisites and direct actions. Verify keyboard access, responsive views and authorization failures.
```

Preserve legacy NeroCD routes during the supported migration window. Do not expose a shortcut that bypasses target, secret, approval or data-ownership rules.

```text
R68. Evidence and releases. A capability is complete when schema, API, permissions, audit, UI, operational behavior and tests agree. Publish supported OS, architecture, Docker/tool versions and measured limits. Use candidate-specific checks and runtime evidence. Do not claim performance gains from choosing Go without measurement.
```

```text
R81. Qualified isolation profiles. Run untrusted code in a supported VM boundary, with an explicit host/kernel/backend/guest-image support matrix, patch/update policy and resource controls. Distinguish task, preview and production boundaries. Use disposable guest disks for ephemeral work and explicit bindings for retained data. Never claim that VM isolation makes arbitrary malicious code harmless. Native Mac, Windows and Linux implementations require their own tests. A WSL distribution alone is not a qualifying VM isolation boundary. GPU/host-device access needs a separate qualified profile. W13
```

```text
R82. Filesystem and network grants. Deny access to personal home directories, host management interfaces, host Docker sockets, personal SSH agents and private networks unless explicitly granted for the task. Enforce network policy outside the untrusted guest, including IPv4/IPv6, host/private/metadata ranges, proxy paths and address revalidation after DNS resolution. Grant specific destinations, ports and data mounts with modes and lifetimes. An ingress tunnel only exposes authorized services and must not become a general LAN route. Revocation behavior must be exercised.
```

```text
R85. Human production authorization. Agent-produced changes require an authorized human decision over the concrete production plan after required checks. Enforce this at the application boundary for UI, CLI, MCP, repository automation and webhooks. Agents cannot change protected deployment policy or replace trusted checks to authorize themselves. A reviewed merge may satisfy the human decision only under an explicit policy that binds the accepted source/artifact, required evidence and final target plan; an unrelated historical PR approval is insufficient. Content or target changes require a new decision.
```

```text
R87. Effective build inputs. Freeze a canonical build input manifest including effective context bytes after ignore rules, relevant named contexts, Dockerfile/frontend, target, platform, resolved base identities, builder/toolchain version, effective build settings, dependency material and output-affecting secret generations. Include submodule/LFS material where used. Retain source lineage separately from content equivalence. A live mutable checkout MUST NOT change while its candidate input is being captured without detection and retry.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l625-l625"></a>

```text
R88. Conservative artifact reuse. Reuse an existing authorized artifact only when the manifest and refresh policy establish eligibility, the artifact is available with its expected identity, and current policy permits it. Unknown mutable external inputs require a declared freshness bound or disable complete-artifact reuse. Freshness-based reuse does not prove those external inputs remained unchanged. A matching Git SHA is insufficient. Record why reuse was accepted or refused and retain original provenance. Force rebuild, mutable-input refresh and check rerun are separate operations.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l627-l627"></a>

```text
R89. Cache trust and transport. Qualify registry-backed build-result caching first. Scope read and write permissions separately by team/project/trust class. Untrusted contributions MUST NOT overwrite a protected cache reference or supply authoritative check results. Prefer immutable per-run exports and controlled shared-reference updates. Warn that caches can contain private build material and apply the same disclosure boundary as source. Distinguish shared layer results from builder-local compiler/package cache mounts. Cache eviction MUST NOT delete pinned releases or backups. W5, W6
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l629-l629"></a>

```text
R90. Required checks and reuse. Every check result records its exact source/artifact subject, definition version, execution environment/platform, time, outcome and retained evidence. Trusted policy chooses mandatory checks. Agent-edited tests can be useful additional evidence but cannot silently redefine the deployment gate. Runtime checks must execute the release artifact. Reuse of successful checks requires matching source/artifact subjects, check-definition and trusted-policy versions, fixtures, relevant environment and freshness criteria. Security or policy changes may require re-verification without rebuilding.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l631-l631"></a>

```text
R91. Platform and attestation identity. Record target OS/architecture/variant, native or emulated execution and image index/platform-manifest identities. Display verification coverage per supported platform. Do not infer native correctness on one platform from a result on another. Seal index-embedded attestations before approval of that index, or retain later evidence by immutable references without mutating the approved identity. Deployment selects the approved eligible platform digest and records it. W10, W11
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l633-l633"></a>

```text
R92. Artifact availability and retention. Publish through authorized, bounded transfers with digest verification and explicit completion state. Candidate publication and deployment MUST NOT claim an artifact exists when required uploads failed. Protect artifacts referenced by retained releases, active deployments and required evidence, with separate cache and checkpoint policies. Reconcile registry/object-store retention and garbage collection. Report unavailable/corrupt artifacts and require a new build/approval where recovery changes their identity. Qualify any self-hosted storage/registry combination before advertising its guarantees.
```

<a id="source-09a432407c41671517fa342d28c07e9c79978aea-69491bd7836f8752eade5799365cbd6fbee8e51eb5e65998687abb35b75b8158-l716-l716"></a>

```text
func TestHostingApplicationDatabaseRouteFailuresCompiledRunner(t *testing.T) {
	testHostingApplicationDatabaseRouteFailuresCompiledRunner(t, false)
}

func testHostingApplicationDatabaseRouteFailuresCompiledRunner(t *testing.T, storage bool) {
	if os.Getenv("NEROCD_HOSTING_DATABASE_RUNNER_RUNTIME") != "disposable-dind" || os.Getenv("NEROCD_DATABASE_CONNECTION_ROUTES") != "1" {
		t.Skip("requires approved combined route fixture profile")
	}
	image := os.Getenv("NEROCD_DATABASE_HTTP_APP_IMAGE")
	if storage {
		image = os.Getenv("NEROCD_DATABASE_STORAGE_HTTP_APP_IMAGE")
	}
	if runtime.GOOS != "linux" || runtime.GOARCH != "arm64" || applicationDatabaseFixtureImage(image) != nil {
		t.Fatal("route failures require native owned image fixture")
	}
	for _, engine := range []string{"postgresql", "redis"} {

			completed := false

				scenario := failure
				if storage {
					scenario = "storage_" + failure
				}
				view := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingDatabase](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/databases", applicationDatabaseRouteFailureCreateInput(engine, scenario, f.environment, f.destination), 201)
				f.registerRouteDatabaseCleanup(view.Resource.ID)
				f.stop()
				source := f.deploy(view, "route_failure_source")
				f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(source.ID)
				f.start()
				f.await(source.ID)
				resource := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.Resource](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources", app.ResourceInput{ProjectID: "proj_platform", ProjectEnvironmentID: f.environment, Name: "route failure " + engine, Kind: "application", Source: domain.ResourceSource{Kind: "image", Image: domain.ImageSource{Reference: image}}}, 201)
				databaseRunnerJSON[domain.ResourceBinding](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/binding", app.ResourceBindingInput{DestinationID: f.destination}, 201)
				namespace := "connected_" + engine
				config := databaseRunnerJSON[struct {
					Configuration domain.HostingRuntimeConfiguration `json:"runtime_configuration"`
				}](f, f.token, "PUT", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/runtime-configuration", domain.HostingRuntimeConfigurationInput{ExpectedResourceGeneration: resource.Generation, ExpectedRuntimeGeneration: 0, RequestID: strings.Repeat("a", 32), Entries: []domain.HostingRuntimeEntry{{Name: "FIXTURE_DATABASE_ENGINE", Kind: "literal", Value: &engine}, {Name: "FIXTURE_DATABASE_NAMESPACE", Kind: "literal", Value: &namespace}}}, 200).Configuration
				deploy := domain.HostingDeploymentInput{ExpectedGeneration: resource.Generation, ExpectedRuntimeConfigurationGeneration: config.RuntimeGeneration, IdempotencyKey: "route_failure_a", ContainerPort: 8080, Readiness: domain.HostingReadiness{Path: "/ready", TimeoutSeconds: 10}}
				f.stop()
				connection := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingDatabaseConnection](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/database-connections", domain.HostingDatabaseConnectionInput{Binding: domain.HostingDatabaseBindingInput{DatabaseResourceID: view.Resource.ID, ExpectedResourceGeneration: resource.Generation, ExpectedRuntimeGeneration: config.RuntimeGeneration, ExpectedDatabaseGeneration: view.Resource.Generation, RequestID: strings.Repeat("b", 32)}, Deployment: deploy}, 202)
				f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(connection.UpgradeOperationID)
				f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(connection.ApplicationOperationID)
				f.start()
				active := f.activeConnection(resource.ID)
				a := f.awaitConnectionOperation(connection.ApplicationOperationID)
				if f.storage != nil {
					a = f.storage.bootstrap(f, resource, a, deploy)
					active = f.connection(resource.ID)
				}
				f.appRecord(a, "PUT", "a", "retained_a")
				r := f.initialApplicationDatabaseRoute(a, engine, roots, public)
				if f.storage != nil {
					f.storage.write(f, a, "retained_a", 11)
				}
				before := f.applicationContainer(a)
				f.stop()
				deploy.IdempotencyKey = "route_failure_b"
				deploy.ExpectedRuntimeConfigurationGeneration = a.Snapshot.RuntimeConfiguration.Generation
				if failure == "readiness" {
					deploy.Readiness = domain.HostingReadiness{Path: "/never-ready", TimeoutSeconds: 3}
					if storage {
						deploy.Readiness.Path = "/fixture-write-then-unready"
					}
				}
				input := r.deployment(deploy)
				if f.storage != nil {
					input = f.storage.deployment(f, input)
				}
				candidate := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingOperation](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/database-connection/deployments", input, 202)
				f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(candidate.ID)
				var wire *applicationDatabaseRouteYieldWire
				if failure == "cutover" {
					wire = newApplicationDatabaseRouteYieldWire(candidate.ID)
					f.routeYield.Store(wire)
				}
				f.start()
				deadline := time.Now().Add(120 * time.Second)
				var staged domain.HostingApplicationDatabaseStage
				for {
					row, err := sqlcgen.New(f.database).ReadApplicationDatabaseStage(t.Context(), candidate.ID)
					exit := f.process.status()
					if err == nil && json.Unmarshal(row.Stage, &staged) == nil {
						var public *applicationDatabaseStoragePublic
						if storage && failure == "readiness" {
							p := f.storage.public(f, candidate.ID)
							public = &p
						}
						if applicationDatabaseRouteProfileFailureObserved(storage, failure, staged, public, exit) {
							break
						}
					}
					if time.Now().After(deadline) || exit.Exited {
						t.Fatal("route failure candidate did not reach exact expected stage")
					}
					select {
					case <-t.Context().Done():
						t.Fatal("route failure wait canceled")
					case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
					}
				}
				if wire != nil {
					ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 30*time.Second)
					reason := waitApplicationDatabaseComplete(ctx, f.process, wire.entered, nil)
					cancel()
					if reason != "" {
						t.Fatal("cutover failure did not commit original ready yield")
					}
				}
				if storage && failure == "readiness" {
					f.awaitSourceJournalRetired()
				}
				f.stop()
				if wire != nil {
					select {
					case <-wire.finished:
					case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
						t.Fatal("cutover fault handler did not join")
					}
				}
				op, err := f.operation(t.Context(), candidate.ID)
				if err != nil || op.Plan == nil || op.Release == nil || op.ApplicationDatabase == nil || staged.Candidate.ContainerID == "" || !storage && (op.Result != nil || op.CompleteReceipt != nil) {
					t.Fatal("route failure exact candidate identity unavailable")
				}
				proof, err := domain.HostingApplicationDatabaseExecutionPlanInput(*op.ApplicationDatabase)
				if err != nil || staged.Validate(*op.Plan, proof) != nil {
					t.Fatal("route failure stage does not match exact operation, plan and endpoint proof")
				}
				if failure == "readiness" && !storage && (op.ApplicationDatabaseYield != nil || applicationDatabaseRouteReadinessRejected(t.Context(), op.Snapshot, staged.Candidate.ContainerID) != nil) {
					t.Fatal("readiness failure yielded or lacks exact candidate HTTP rejection")
				}
				if storage {
					f.storage.recoverFailure(f, engine, failure, resource, view, a, op, staged, active, wire)
					fmt.Println("DATABASE_CONNECTION_STORAGE_RECOVERY_PASS " + engine + " " + failure)
					return
				}
				if failure == "cutover" {
					// Recheck exact create labels and image before the deliberate stop.
					var actual databaseRunnerContainer
					if json.Unmarshal(f.docker("inspect", staged.Candidate.ContainerID, "--format", `{"Id":{{json .Id}},"Image":{{json .Image}},"Config":{"Labels":{{json .Config.Labels}}},"State":{{json .State}}}`), &actual) != nil || actual.ID != staged.Candidate.ContainerID || actual.Image != op.Release.ImageID || !actual.State.Running || actual.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.operation"] != op.ID || actual.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.binding"] != op.BindingID || actual.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.plan"] != op.Plan.Hash {
						t.Fatal("cutover stop target identity changed")
					}
					f.docker("stop", "--time", "1", staged.Candidate.ContainerID)
					public := databaseRunnerJSON[struct {
						Continuity struct {
							ProxyOperationID string `json:"proxy_operation_id"`
						} `json:"application_database_route_continuity"`
					}](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/hosting-operations/"+candidate.ID, nil, 200)
					if public.Continuity.ProxyOperationID == "" {
						t.Fatal("cutover failure proxy identity absent")
					}
					f.start()
					deadline = time.Now().Add(120 * time.Second)
					for {
						proxy := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingProxyOperationView](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/route-switches/"+public.Continuity.ProxyOperationID, nil, 200)
						if proxy.State == "rolled_back" && proxy.EngineOutcome == "rolled_back" {
							break
						}
						if time.Now().After(deadline) || f.process.status().Exited {
							t.Fatal("strict cutover failure did not prove rollback")
						}
						select {
						case <-t.Context().Done():
							t.Fatal("rollback wait canceled")
						case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
						}
					}
					f.stop()
				}
				r.assertSelected(a)
				r.record(t.Context(), a, "GET", "a", "retained_a")
				r.record(t.Context(), a, "PUT", "after_failure", "retained_after_failure")
				r.record(t.Context(), a, "GET", "after_failure", "retained_after_failure")
				if !reflect.DeepEqual(before, f.applicationContainer(a)) {
					t.Fatal("failure changed exact old app identity or endpoint")
				}
				current := f.connection(resource.ID)
				failed, failedErr := f.operation(t.Context(), candidate.ID)
				if failedErr != nil || failed.State == "succeeded" || !failed.MutationHold || current.HoldOperationID != candidate.ID {
					t.Fatal("failed routed candidate falsely settled or released its safety holds")
				}
				var healthy string
				if current.MembershipRevision != active.MembershipRevision || f.database.QueryRow(t.Context(), `SELECT healthy->>'operation_id' FROM hosting_binding_state WHERE binding_id=$1`, a.BindingID).Scan(&healthy) != nil || healthy != a.ID {
					t.Fatal("failure settled candidate as healthy or active database member")
				}
				var retirements int
				if f.database.QueryRow(t.Context(), `SELECT count(*) FROM hosting_application_database_retirements WHERE operation_id=$1`, candidate.ID).Scan(&retirements) != nil || retirements != 0 {
					t.Fatal("failure retired old app")
				}
				fmt.Println("DATABASE_CONNECTION_ROUTE_FAILURE_PASS " + engine + " " + failure)
			}) {
				return
			}
			if !completed {
				continue
			}
			applicationDatabaseRouteCapacity(t)
			if storage {
				fmt.Println("DATABASE_CONNECTION_STORAGE_CAPACITY_PASS " + engine + " " + failure)
			} else {
				fmt.Println("DATABASE_CONNECTION_ROUTE_CAPACITY_PASS " + engine + " " + failure)
			}
		}
	}
}
```
