```text
			failureReason = reason
			f.t.Fatal("storage recovery did not independently prove successful settlement: " + reason)
		}
		select {
		case <-f.t.Context().Done():
			failureReason = "wait_canceled"
			f.t.Fatal("storage recovery wait canceled")
		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
		}
	}
	f.stop()
	phase = "runtime_validation"
	selected := previous
	var maintained domain.HostingOperation
	if action == "resume_predecessor" {
		settled := s.public(f, op.ID)
		if settled.State != original.State || !reflect.DeepEqual(settled.Result, original.Result) {
			f.t.Fatal("resume recovery rewrote original failed operation outcome")
		}
		f.applicationContainer(previous)
		// Successful inventories, rather than an inspect error, prove the exact
		// failed B is absent while A uses the original retained volume.
		for _, filter := range []string{"id=" + stage.Candidate.ContainerID, "label=io.nerocd.operation=" + op.ID} {
			if strings.TrimSpace(string(f.docker("container", "ls", "--all", "--quiet", "--no-trunc", "--filter", filter))) != "" {
				f.t.Fatal("resume left the proven-stopped failed candidate container behind")
			}
		}
		s.assertFiles(f, previous)
		r.assertSelected(previous)
		r.record(f.t.Context(), previous, "GET", "a", "retained_a")
		r.record(f.t.Context(), previous, "GET", "candidate_write", "retained_candidate_before_recovery")
		writers := strings.Fields(string(f.docker("container", "ls", "--quiet", "--no-trunc", "--filter", "volume="+s.Plan.VolumeName)))
		if len(writers) != 1 || writers[0] != previous.Result.ContainerID {
			f.t.Fatal("resumed predecessor is not the sole running volume writer")
		}
		resumed := f.connection(op.ResourceID)
		if resumed.State != "active" || resumed.HoldOperationID != "" || resumed.MembershipRevision <= active.MembershipRevision {
			f.t.Fatal("resumed connection lacks fresh endpoint membership revision or retained holds")
		}
		s.assertResumeMembership(f, op, previous, stage, run, active.MembershipRevision, resumed.MembershipRevision)
		oldDatabase, err := f.operation(f.t.Context(), op.ApplicationDatabase.DatabaseHealthy.OperationID)
		if err != nil || oldDatabase.Plan == nil || oldDatabase.Result == nil {
			f.t.Fatal("resumed database maintenance predecessor unavailable")
		}
		databaseVolume, credentials := f.volumeProof(oldDatabase), f.credentialMetadata(database)
		maintenance := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingOperation](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+database.Resource.ID+"/database/maintenance", domain.HostingDatabaseMaintenanceInput{ExpectedGeneration: database.Resource.Generation, ExpectedMembershipRevision: resumed.MembershipRevision, IdempotencyKey: "storage_resume_database_maintenance"}, 202)
		f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(maintenance.ID)
		f.start()
		maintained = f.awaitConnectionOperation(maintenance.ID)
		f.stop()
		if f.volumeProof(maintained) != databaseVolume || f.credentialMetadata(database) != credentials {
			f.t.Fatal("database maintenance after resume changed retained database identity")
		}
		proof := s.public(f, op.ID)
		if maintained.Plan.Database.Network == nil || maintained.Plan.Database.Network.MembershipRevision != resumed.MembershipRevision || len(maintained.Plan.Database.Network.Members) != 1 {
			f.t.Fatal("database maintenance did not compile resumed membership revision")
		}
		member := maintained.Plan.Database.Network.Members[0]
		actualApp := f.applicationContainer(previous)
		if member.ReceiptID != proof.StorageState.ReceiptID || member.ReceiptHash != proof.StorageState.StateHash || member.Endpoint.Target != op.ApplicationDatabase.Members[0].EndpointPlan.Target || member.Endpoint.EndpointID != actualApp.Endpoints[op.ApplicationDatabase.Binding.NetworkName].EndpointID {
			f.t.Fatal("database maintenance did not consume exact fresh recovery receipt and observed endpoint")
		}
		f.inspect(maintained)
		var members map[string]json.RawMessage
		if json.Unmarshal(f.docker("network", "inspect", previous.ApplicationDatabase.Origin.NetworkID, "--format", "{{json .Containers}}"), &members) != nil || len(members) != 2 || members[previous.Result.ContainerID] == nil || members[maintained.Result.ContainerID] == nil {
			f.t.Fatal("maintenance after resume did not preserve exact active application/database endpoints")
		}
		s.assertFiles(f, previous)
		r.record(f.t.Context(), previous, "GET", "candidate_write", "retained_candidate_before_recovery")
		r.record(f.t.Context(), previous, "PUT", "resumed_maintenance", "retained_after_resume_maintenance")
	} else {
		current, err := f.operation(f.t.Context(), op.ID)
		if err != nil || !applicationDatabaseCompleted(current) || current.Result.ContainerID != stage.Candidate.ContainerID || current.ApplicationDatabaseRouteContinuity.ProxyOperationID != failedProxy.ID {
			f.t.Fatal("forward recovery did not finalize the exact original candidate and failed-P identity")
		}
		p2 := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingProxyOperationView](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/resources/"+op.ResourceID+"/route-switches/"+proxyID, nil, 200)
		old := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingProxyOperationView](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/resources/"+op.ResourceID+"/route-switches/"+failedProxy.ID, nil, 200)
		if p2.ID != proxyID || p2.State != "applied" || p2.EngineOutcome != "applied" || old.State != failedProxy.State || old.EngineOutcome != failedProxy.EngineOutcome {
			f.t.Fatal("forward recovery lost immutable failed P or exact applied P2")
		}
		r.assertSelected(current)
		s.assertFiles(f, current)
		r.record(f.t.Context(), current, "GET", "a", "retained_a")
		r.record(f.t.Context(), current, "GET", "candidate_write", "retained_candidate_before_recovery")
		s.write(f, current, "recovered", 44)
		f.assertApplicationDatabaseRetirement(current, previous)
		selected = current
	}
	phase = "authority_validation"
	var leases, targets int
	if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT count(*) FROM run_leases l JOIN task_runs r ON r.id=l.run_id WHERE l.run_id=$1 AND l.status='succeeded' AND l.attempt=1 AND l.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND r.status='succeeded' AND r.finished_at IS NOT NULL AND l.runner_id=$2 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM run_leases original WHERE original.run_id=$3 AND (original.id=l.id OR original.fence=l.fence))`, run, op.Snapshot.RunnerID, op.RunID).Scan(&leases) != nil || leases != 1 {
		f.t.Fatal("storage recovery lacks exact fresh succeeded run/lease/fence independent of original prepare authority")
	}
	if action == "resume_predecessor" {
		if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT count(*) FROM hosting_task_targets t JOIN task_runs r ON r.id=t.run_id WHERE t.run_id=$1 AND t.operation_id=$2 AND t.binding_id=$3 AND t.runner_id=$4 AND r.run_spec->>'hosting_operation_id'=t.operation_id AND r.run_spec->>'hosting_mode'=t.mode`, run, op.ID, op.BindingID, op.Snapshot.RunnerID).Scan(&targets) != nil || targets != 1 {
			f.t.Fatal("resume recovery run is not targeted at exact original application")
		}
	} else if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT count(*) FROM hosting_proxy_task_targets WHERE run_id=$1 AND operation_id=$2 AND proxy_id=$3 AND runner_id=$4 AND mode='apply'`, run, proxyID, r.proxy.ID, op.Snapshot.RunnerID).Scan(&targets) != nil || targets != 1 {
		f.t.Fatal("forward recovery run is not targeted at exact fresh proxy")
	}
	r.assertUnrelated()
	if browser != nil {
		phase = "browser_validation"
		browser.advance("finish", f.connection(op.ResourceID).MembershipRevision, selected, map[string]string{"a": "retained_a", "candidate_write": "retained_candidate_before_recovery"})
		browser.awaitFinished()
		fmt.Println("DATABASE_CONNECTION_STORAGE_RECOVERY_UI_PASS " + engine + " " + action)
	}
	if action == "resume_predecessor" {
		// Recovery UI observes the resumed A first. A fresh API deployment then
		// proves the recovered membership can retire A and settle new C normally.
		phase = "resume_redeploy"
		request := s.requestResumedReplacement(f, resource, previous)
		f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(request.ID)
		revision := f.connection(resource.ID).MembershipRevision
		r.recoverYield(request, previous, revision)
		current := f.awaitConnectionOperation(request.ID)
		f.stop()
		if current.ID == op.ID || current.ID == previous.ID || current.Result.ContainerID == stage.Candidate.ContainerID || current.Result.ContainerID == previous.Result.ContainerID || current.Result.PreviousContainerID != previous.Result.ContainerID {
			f.t.Fatal("resumed replacement reused failed B or did not replace exact recovered A")
		}
		f.assertApplicationDatabaseRetirement(current, previous)
		f.exactMembers(current, maintained)
		r.assertSelected(current)
		s.assertFiles(f, current)
		for key, value := range map[string]string{"a": "retained_a", "candidate_write": "retained_candidate_before_recovery", "resumed_maintenance": "retained_after_resume_maintenance"} {
			r.record(f.t.Context(), current, "GET", key, value)
		}
		s.write(f, current, "retained_c", 55)
		r.record(f.t.Context(), current, "PUT", "after_resume_redeploy", "retained_after_resume_redeploy")
		r.record(f.t.Context(), current, "GET", "after_resume_redeploy", "retained_after_resume_redeploy")
		originalAfter := s.public(f, op.ID)
		if originalAfter.State != original.State || !reflect.DeepEqual(originalAfter.Result, original.Result) || originalAfter.StorageState.RecoveryState != "succeeded" {
			f.t.Fatal("new deployment rewrote original failure or recovery settlement")
		}
		f.assertConnectionJournalRetired(current.ID)
		r.assertUnrelated()
		f.t.Log("resumed A replaced by fresh C with exact retained database/upload identity and trusted HTTPS writes")
	}
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) assertResumeMembership(f *databaseRunnerFixture, op, previous domain.HostingOperation, stage domain.HostingApplicationDatabaseStage, run string, before, after int64) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if len(op.ApplicationDatabase.Members) != 1 || after != before+1 {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed membership did not advance exactly once")
	}
	head, err := sqlcgen.New(f.database).ReadDatabaseMembershipHead(f.t.Context(), op.ApplicationDatabase.Binding.DatabaseBindingID)
	var members []json.RawMessage
	if err != nil || head.Revision != after || json.Unmarshal(head.Members, &members) != nil || len(members) != 1 {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed membership head unavailable")
	}
	var current struct {
		Resume *struct {
			Version             string          `json:"version"`
			OperationID         string          `json:"operation_id"`
			MembershipRevision  int64           `json:"membership_revision"`
			OriginalReceiptHash string          `json:"original_receipt_hash"`
			WriterReceipt       json.RawMessage `json:"writer_receipt"`
		} `json:"resume"`
	}
	var raw []byte
	if json.Unmarshal(members[0], &current) != nil || current.Resume == nil || f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT request FROM hosting_application_database_storage_writers WHERE operation_id=$1 AND phase='resumed'`, op.ID).Scan(&raw) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed writer or fresh membership receipt absent")
	}
	defer clear(raw)
	var writer struct {
		domain.HostingAuthority
		Receipt json.RawMessage `json:"receipt"`
	}
	var receipt struct {
		Version             string                                            `json:"version"`
		Phase               string                                            `json:"phase"`
		PredecessorEndpoint *domain.HostingDatabaseBindingEndpointObservation `json:"predecessor_endpoint"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &writer) != nil || json.Unmarshal(writer.Receipt, &receipt) != nil || writer.OperationID != op.ID || writer.RunID != run || writer.LeaseID == "" || writer.Fence == "" || writer.Attempt != 1 || receipt.Version != applicationDatabaseStorageVersion || receipt.Phase != "resumed" || receipt.PredecessorEndpoint == nil {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed receipt lacks exact fresh recovery authority or actual endpoint observation")
	}
	// Decode the narrowed fields by their wire names; the full immutable receipt
	// is compared below without inventing a replacement proof or hash.
	var wireReceipt struct {
		ReceiptID string `json:"receipt_id"`
		Hash      string `json:"hash"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(writer.Receipt, &wireReceipt) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed receipt identity invalid")
	}
	old := op.ApplicationDatabase.Members[0]
	r := current.Resume
	var a, b map[string]any
	if json.Unmarshal(r.WriterReceipt, &a) != nil || json.Unmarshal(writer.Receipt, &b) != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(a, b) || r.Version != applicationDatabaseStorageVersion || r.OperationID != op.ID || r.MembershipRevision != after || r.OriginalReceiptHash != old.Receipt.Hash {
		f.t.Fatal("fresh membership does not pin original attachment and exact resumed receipt")
	}
	var actual, historical map[string]any
	oldRaw, _ := json.Marshal(old)
	if json.Unmarshal(members[0], &actual) != nil || json.Unmarshal(oldRaw, &historical) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed membership history unavailable")
	}
	delete(actual, "resume")
	delete(historical, "resume")
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(actual, historical) {
		f.t.Fatal("resume rewrote historical application, attachment or database evidence")
	}
	endpoint := receipt.PredecessorEndpoint.Endpoint
	inspection := f.applicationContainer(previous)
	if !receipt.PredecessorEndpoint.Present || endpoint.Target != old.EndpointPlan.Target || endpoint.EndpointID == old.Receipt.Observation.Endpoint.EndpointID || endpoint.EndpointID != inspection.Endpoints[op.ApplicationDatabase.Binding.NetworkName].EndpointID {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed endpoint differs from exact restarted container or reused stale attachment")
	}
	public := s.public(f, op.ID)
	if public.StorageState.ReceiptID != wireReceipt.ReceiptID || public.StorageState.StateHash != wireReceipt.Hash {
		f.t.Fatal("public resumed state differs from durable writer receipt")
	}
	var membership []byte
	a, b = nil, nil
	if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT body FROM hosting_application_database_storage_membership_receipts WHERE database_binding_id=$1 AND revision=$2 AND operation_id=$3`, op.ApplicationDatabase.Binding.DatabaseBindingID, after, op.ID).Scan(&membership) != nil || json.Unmarshal(membership, &a) != nil || json.Unmarshal(members[0], &b) != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(a, b) {
		f.t.Fatal("resumed head lacks separate exact immutable membership receipt")
	}
	retained, err := sqlcgen.New(f.database).ReadApplicationDatabaseStage(f.t.Context(), op.ID)
	var oldStage domain.HostingApplicationDatabaseStage
	if err != nil || json.Unmarshal(retained.Stage, &oldStage) != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(oldStage, stage) || databaseUpgradeAuthorityLogCheck(f.logs.snapshot(), writer.HostingAuthority, f.protected) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("resume changed original stage or exposed recovery authority")
	}
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) bootstrap(f *databaseRunnerFixture, resource domain.Resource, previous domain.HostingOperation, deployment domain.HostingDeploymentInput) domain.HostingOperation {
	f.t.Helper()
	s.Metadata = databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingStorage](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/storage", domain.HostingStorageInput{RequestID: domain.HostingDocumentHash(struct{ Resource, Profile string }{resource.ID, "connected_storage_success"})[7:39], ExpectedResourceGeneration: resource.Generation, MountPath: "/data/uploads"}, 201)
	if s.Metadata.Validate() != nil || s.Metadata.ResourceID != resource.ID || s.Metadata.BindingID != previous.BindingID || s.Metadata.MountPath != "/data/uploads" {
		f.t.Fatal("connected upload metadata differs from exact application binding")
	}
	f.stop()
	deployment.ExpectedRuntimeConfigurationGeneration = previous.Snapshot.RuntimeConfiguration.Generation
	deployment.IdempotencyKey = "connected_storage_bootstrap"
	request := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingOperation](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/resources/"+resource.ID+"/database-connection/deployments", s.deployment(f, deployment), 202)
	f.registerRouteOperationCleanup(request.ID)
	f.start()
	current := f.awaitConnectionOperation(request.ID)
	if current.Plan.Storage == nil || current.Plan.Storage.Reference != (domain.HostingStorageRef{StorageID: s.Metadata.ID, Generation: s.Metadata.Generation, Hash: s.Metadata.Hash}) || current.Plan.Storage.VolumeName != s.Metadata.VolumeName || current.Plan.Storage.CreationOperationID != current.ID {
		f.t.Fatal("bootstrap did not materialize exact application-owned upload volume")
	}
	copy := *current.Plan.Storage
	s.Plan = &copy
	s.VolumeProof = f.volumeProof(current)
	var volume struct{ Labels map[string]string }
	materialization := domain.HostingStorageMaterialization{CreationOperationID: current.ID, CreationPlanHash: current.Plan.Hash, CreationNonce: copy.CreationNonce, DaemonID: copy.DaemonID}
	if json.Unmarshal([]byte(s.VolumeProof), &volume) != nil || !maps.Equal(volume.Labels, domain.ExpectedHostingStorageLabels(s.Metadata, materialization)) {
		f.t.Fatal("initial upload volume labels differ from exact owned creation provenance")
	}
	f.applicationContainer(current)
	f.assertApplicationDatabaseRetirement(current, previous)
	return current
}

func applicationDatabaseStorageStopBeforeStart(oldRunning, nextRunning bool, stopped, started string) bool {
	a, errA := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, stopped)
	b, errB := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, started)
	return !oldRunning && nextRunning && errA == nil && errB == nil && !a.IsZero() && !b.IsZero() && !a.After(b)
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) assertTransition(f *databaseRunnerFixture, previous, candidate domain.HostingOperation) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if s.Plan == nil || candidate.Plan == nil || candidate.Plan.Storage == nil || *candidate.Plan.Storage != *s.Plan || previous.Plan == nil || previous.Plan.Storage == nil || *previous.Plan.Storage != *s.Plan {
		f.t.Fatal("one-writer transition changed exact retained volume origin")
	}
	old, stopped, _ := s.inspectWriter(f, previous)
	next, _, started := s.inspectWriter(f, candidate)
	if !applicationDatabaseStorageStopBeforeStart(old.State.Running, next.State.Running, stopped, started) {
		f.t.Fatal("previous application was not independently proven stopped before candidate start")
	}
	writers := strings.Fields(string(f.docker("container", "ls", "--quiet", "--no-trunc", "--filter", "volume="+s.Plan.VolumeName)))
	if len(writers) != 1 || writers[0] != candidate.Result.ContainerID {
		f.t.Fatal("retained upload volume has an extra or missing running writer")
	}
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) inspectWriter(f *databaseRunnerFixture, op domain.HostingOperation) (databaseRunnerContainer, string, string) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if s.Plan == nil || op.Plan == nil || op.Plan.Storage == nil || *op.Plan.Storage != *s.Plan || op.Result == nil || op.Release == nil {
		f.t.Fatal("writer observation lacks exact retained plan and container identity")
	}
	raw := f.docker("container", "inspect", op.Result.ContainerID, "--format", `{"Id":{{json .Id}},"Image":{{json .Image}},"Config":{"Labels":{{json .Config.Labels}}},"State":{{json .State}},"Mounts":{{json .Mounts}}}`)
	var c databaseRunnerContainer
	var state struct {
		State struct{ FinishedAt, StartedAt string }
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &c) != nil || json.Unmarshal(raw, &state) != nil || c.ID != op.Result.ContainerID || c.Image != op.Release.ImageID || c.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.binding"] != op.BindingID || c.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.operation"] != op.ID || c.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.plan"] != op.Plan.Hash || c.Config.Labels["io.nerocd.release"] != op.Release.Hash || !applicationDatabaseStorageMount(c, s.Plan) {
		f.t.Fatal("one-writer observation lacks exact container, image, labels or mount")
	}
	return c, state.State.FinishedAt, state.State.StartedAt
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) assertReadinessStopped(f *databaseRunnerFixture, previous, candidate domain.HostingOperation, stage domain.HostingApplicationDatabaseStage) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if candidate.State != "failed" || candidate.ApplicationDatabaseYield != nil || candidate.CompleteReceipt != nil || !candidate.MutationHold || stage.Phase != "attached" {
		f.t.Fatal("storage readiness failure lost exact failed operation or safety hold")
	}
	old, oldFinished, _ := s.inspectWriter(f, previous)
	next, finished, started := s.inspectWriter(f, candidate)
	stopA, errA := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, oldFinished)
	startB, errB := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, started)
	stopB, errC := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, finished)
	if old.State.Running || next.State.Running || errA != nil || errB != nil || errC != nil || stopA.IsZero() || startB.IsZero() || stopB.IsZero() || stopA.After(startB) || startB.After(stopB) {
		f.t.Fatal("storage readiness failure did not independently prove A then B stopped")
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(string(f.docker("container", "ls", "--quiet", "--no-trunc", "--filter", "volume="+s.Plan.VolumeName))) != "" || f.volumeProof(candidate) != s.VolumeProof {
		f.t.Fatal("failed readiness retained a running volume writer or changed volume identity")
	}
	var total int
	if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT count(*) FROM hosting_application_database_storage_writers WHERE operation_id=$1`, candidate.ID).Scan(&total) != nil || total != 4 {
		f.t.Fatal("failed readiness lacks exact ordered stop and failure receipt cardinality")
	}
	var authority domain.HostingAuthority
	prior, observation, lastReceipt := "", "", ""
	for i, phase := range []string{"stop_intent", "stopped", "candidate_stopped", "replacement_failed"} {
		var raw []byte
		if f.database.QueryRow(f.t.Context(), `SELECT request FROM hosting_application_database_storage_writers WHERE operation_id=$1 AND phase=$2`, candidate.ID, phase).Scan(&raw) != nil || len(raw) > 32768 {
			f.t.Fatal("failed readiness writer receipt unavailable")
		}
		var request struct {
			domain.HostingAuthority
			Receipt struct {
				Version           string                   `json:"version"`
				ReceiptID         string                   `json:"receipt_id"`
				Phase             string                   `json:"phase"`
				PlanHash          string                   `json:"plan_hash"`
				StorageRef        domain.HostingStorageRef `json:"storage_ref"`
				PreviousStateHash string                   `json:"previous_state_hash"`
				StageHash         string                   `json:"stage_hash"`
				CandidateHash     string                   `json:"candidate_hash"`
				PredecessorHash   string                   `json:"predecessor_hash"`
				ObservationHash   string                   `json:"observation_hash"`
				Hash              string                   `json:"hash"`
			} `json:"receipt"`
		}
		err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &request)
		clear(raw)
		receipt := request.Receipt
		if i == 0 {
			authority = request.HostingAuthority
		}
		if err != nil || request.HostingAuthority != authority || authority.OperationID != candidate.ID || authority.RunID != candidate.RunID || authority.LeaseID == "" || authority.Fence == "" || authority.Attempt < 1 || receipt.Version != applicationDatabaseStorageVersion || receipt.Phase != phase || receipt.ReceiptID == "" || receipt.Hash == "" || receipt.PlanHash != candidate.Plan.Hash || receipt.StorageRef != s.Plan.Reference || receipt.PredecessorHash != domain.HostingDocumentHash(candidate.Plan.PreviousHealthy) || receipt.PreviousStateHash != prior {
			f.t.Fatal("failed readiness stop/failure receipt lost exact provenance or hash chain")
		}
		if i >= 2 && (receipt.StageHash != stage.Hash || receipt.CandidateHash != stage.Candidate.Hash || receipt.ObservationHash == "") {
			f.t.Fatal("failed readiness receipt does not identify the exact stopped candidate")
		}
		if i == 2 {
			observation = receipt.ObservationHash
		}
		if i == 3 && receipt.ObservationHash != observation {
			f.t.Fatal("replacement failure does not retain exact candidate-stop observation")
		}
		prior, lastReceipt = receipt.Hash, receipt.ReceiptID
	}
	public := s.public(f, candidate.ID)
	phase, err := f.applicationDatabasePhaseAuthority(authority.LeaseID)
	if err != nil || phase.HostingAuthority != authority || phase.Mode != "deploy" || phase.LeaseStatus != "failed" || phase.TaskStatus != "failed" || phase.CompletionKey != lastReceipt || public.StorageState.StateHash != prior || public.StorageState.ReceiptID != lastReceipt || databaseUpgradeAuthorityLogCheck(f.logs.snapshot(), authority, f.protected) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("failed readiness did not settle original failed task under exact failure receipt")
	}
	f.assertConnectionJournalRetired(candidate.ID)
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) deployment(f *databaseRunnerFixture, input any) any {
	f.t.Helper()
	options := databaseRunnerJSON[struct {
		Review *struct {
			Version                         string `json:"version"`
			Strategy                        string `json:"strategy"`
			ExpectedStorageGeneration       int64  `json:"expected_storage_generation"`
			ExpectedStorageHash             string `json:"expected_storage_hash"`
			AcknowledgeInterruptionRequired bool   `json:"acknowledge_interruption_required"`
		} `json:"application_database_storage"`
	}](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/resources/"+s.Metadata.ResourceID+"/storage-deployment-options", nil, 200)
	r := options.Review
	if r == nil || r.Version != applicationDatabaseStorageVersion || r.Strategy != "replacement_with_interruption" || r.ExpectedStorageGeneration != s.Metadata.Generation || r.ExpectedStorageHash != s.Metadata.Hash || !r.AcknowledgeInterruptionRequired {
		f.t.Fatal("public connected storage review differs from exact saved metadata")
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(input)
	var out map[string]any
	if err != nil || json.Unmarshal(raw, &out) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("connected storage deployment request unavailable")
	}
	out["application_database_storage"] = applicationDatabaseStorageAck{s.Metadata.Generation, s.Metadata.Hash, true}
	return out
}

func applicationDatabaseStoragePayload(seed byte) []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 65537)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(i*31) ^ seed
	}
	return data
}

// The real Docker cp archive is inspected in memory. No archive paths are
// extracted and neither the request nor response can choose a host path.
func applicationDatabaseUploadArchive(raw, expected []byte) error {
	invalid := errors.New("upload archive identity, bounds or metadata invalid")
	if len(raw) > 1<<20 || len(expected) != 65537 {
		return invalid
	}
	reader := tar.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	h, err := reader.Next()
	if err != nil || h.Typeflag != tar.TypeReg || h.Name != "retained_a" || h.Linkname != "" || h.Mode != 0640 || h.Uid != 12345 || h.Gid != 12346 || h.Size != int64(len(expected)) {
		return invalid
	}
	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(reader, 65538))
	defer clear(data)
	if err != nil || len(data) != len(expected) || sha256.Sum256(data) != sha256.Sum256(expected) {
		return invalid
	}
	if _, err := reader.Next(); err != io.EOF {
		return invalid
	}
	return nil
}

func applicationDatabaseUploadDirectoryArchive(raw []byte, files map[string][]byte) error {
	invalid := errors.New("upload directory archive identity, bounds or metadata invalid")
	if len(raw) > 1<<20 || len(files) < 1 || len(files) > 3 {
		return invalid
	}
	reader := tar.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	directory, seen := false, map[string]bool{}
	for range len(files) + 2 {
		h, err := reader.Next()
		if err == io.EOF {
			if directory && len(seen) == len(files) {
				return nil
			}
			return invalid
		}
		if err != nil || h.Linkname != "" || h.Uid != 12345 || h.Gid != 12346 {
			return invalid
		}
		if h.Typeflag == tar.TypeDir && h.Name == "uploads/" && h.Mode == 0750 && !directory {
			directory = true
			continue
		}
		key := strings.TrimPrefix(h.Name, "uploads/")
		data, exists := files[key]
		if !exists || seen[key] || h.Name != "uploads/"+key || h.Typeflag != tar.TypeReg || h.Mode != 0640 || h.Size != int64(len(data)) || len(data) != 65537 {
			return invalid
		}
		actual, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(reader, 65538))
		match := err == nil && len(actual) == len(data) && sha256.Sum256(actual) == sha256.Sum256(data)
		clear(actual)
		if !match {
			return invalid
		}
		seen[key] = true
	}
	return invalid
}

func applicationDatabaseStorageMount(c databaseRunnerContainer, plan *domain.HostingStoragePlan) bool {
	if plan == nil {
		return len(c.Mounts) == 0
	}
	if len(c.Mounts) != 1 || plan.MountPath != "/data/uploads" || plan.VolumeName == "" {
		return false
	}
	m := c.Mounts[0]
	return m.Type == "volume" && m.Name == plan.VolumeName && m.Destination == plan.MountPath && m.RW
}

func applicationDatabaseUpload(ctx context.Context, roots *x509.CertPool, hostname, fingerprint string, op domain.HostingOperation, method, key string, expected []byte, target string) error {
	invalid := errors.New("connected upload identity, trust or content invalid")
	if op.Result == nil || len(op.Result.ContainerID) != 64 || strings.Trim(op.Result.ContainerID, "0123456789abcdef") != "" || len(expected) != 65537 || len(key) == 0 || len(key) > 64 || strings.Trim(key, "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_") != "" || method != "GET" && method != "PUT" {
		return invalid
	}
	transport := &http.Transport{Proxy: nil, DisableKeepAlives: true}
	url := "http://127.0.0.1:" + strconv.Itoa(op.Snapshot.HostPort) + "/uploads/" + key
	if roots != nil {
		canonical, err := domain.NormalizeHostingHostname(hostname)
		ip, port, dialErr := net.SplitHostPort(target)
		if err != nil || canonical != hostname || len(fingerprint) != 64 || strings.Trim(fingerprint, "0123456789abcdef") != "" || dialErr != nil || ip != "127.0.0.1" || port == "" {
			return invalid
		}
		transport.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12, RootCAs: roots}
		transport.DialContext = func(ctx context.Context, _, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
			if address != hostname+":443" {
				return nil, invalid
			}
			return (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext(ctx, "tcp4", target)
		}
		url = "https://" + hostname + "/uploads/" + key
	}
	defer transport.CloseIdleConnections()
	client := &http.Client{Transport: transport, Timeout: 7 * time.Second, CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }}
	var body io.Reader
	if method == "PUT" {
		body = bytes.NewReader(expected)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, url, body)
	if err != nil {
		return invalid
	}
	response, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return invalid
	}
	data, readErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(response.Body, 65538))
	defer clear(data)
	closeErr := response.Body.Close()
	if readErr != nil || closeErr != nil || response.Header.Get("X-NeroCD-Fixture-Instance") != op.Result.ContainerID[:12] {
		return invalid
	}
	if roots != nil {
		if response.TLS == nil || len(response.TLS.VerifiedChains) == 0 || len(response.TLS.PeerCertificates) == 0 {
			return invalid
		}
		hash := sha256.Sum256(response.TLS.PeerCertificates[0].Raw)
		if hex.EncodeToString(hash[:]) != fingerprint {
			return invalid
		}
	}
	if method == "PUT" {
		if response.StatusCode != http.StatusCreated || len(data) != 0 {
			return invalid
		}
	} else if response.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || len(data) != len(expected) || sha256.Sum256(data) != sha256.Sum256(expected) {
		return invalid
	}
	return nil
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) assertFiles(f *databaseRunnerFixture, op domain.HostingOperation) {
	f.t.Helper()
	f.applicationContainer(op)
	if op.Plan.Storage == nil || s.Plan == nil || *op.Plan.Storage != *s.Plan {
		f.t.Fatal("upload volume creation origin changed across replacement")
	}
	if f.volumeProof(op) != s.VolumeProof {
		f.t.Fatal("upload volume daemon metadata or original creation identity changed")
	}
	for key, value := range s.Files {
		if applicationDatabaseUpload(f.t.Context(), nil, "", "", op, "GET", key, value, "") != nil {
			f.t.Fatal("connected retained upload failed direct application read")
		}
		if f.routes != nil && applicationDatabaseUpload(f.t.Context(), f.routes.roots, f.routes.hostname, f.routes.route.Certificate.Fingerprint, op, "GET", key, value, "127.0.0.1:443") != nil {
			f.t.Fatal("connected retained upload failed trusted HTTPS read")
		}
	}
	raw := f.docker("cp", op.Result.ContainerID+":/data/uploads/retained_a", "-")
	if applicationDatabaseUploadArchive(raw, s.Files["retained_a"]) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("retained upload digest or 0640 ownership proof failed")
	}
	if applicationDatabaseUploadDirectoryArchive(f.docker("cp", op.Result.ContainerID+":/data/uploads", "-"), s.Files) != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("retained upload directory 0750 ownership, contents or digest proof failed")
	}
}

func (s *applicationDatabaseStorageFixture) write(f *databaseRunnerFixture, op domain.HostingOperation, key string, seed byte) {
	f.t.Helper()
	data := applicationDatabaseStoragePayload(seed)
	var err error
	if f.routes != nil {
		err = applicationDatabaseUpload(f.t.Context(), f.routes.roots, f.routes.hostname, f.routes.route.Certificate.Fingerprint, op, "PUT", key, data, "127.0.0.1:443")
	} else {
		err = applicationDatabaseUpload(f.t.Context(), nil, "", "", op, "PUT", key, data, "")
	}
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal("connected application upload write failed")
	}
	if s.Files == nil {
		s.Files = map[string][]byte{}
	}
	s.Files[key] = data
	s.assertFiles(f, op)
}
```

```text
func TestHostingDatabaseCompiledRunner(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("NEROCD_HOSTING_DATABASE_RUNNER_RUNTIME") != "disposable-dind" {
		t.Skip("run acceptance/runtime-hosting-database-runner/gate.sh after explicit physical authorization")
	}

		t.Fatal("native Linux arm64 required")
	}

	for i, engine := range []string{"postgresql", "redis"} {
		version := domain.HostingDatabasePostgresRecipe
		if engine == "redis" {
			version = domain.HostingDatabaseRedisRecipe
		}
		view := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingDatabase](f, f.token, "POST", "/api/v1/databases", domain.HostingDatabaseCreateInput{RequestID: strings.Repeat(string(rune('a'+i)), 32), ProjectID: "proj_platform", ProjectEnvironmentID: f.environment, Name: "runner fixture " + engine, DestinationID: f.destination, Engine: engine, RecipeVersion: version}, 201)
		if view.RuntimeState != domain.HostingDatabaseUnqualified || len(view.Credentials) != 2 {
			t.Fatal("metadata asserted engine qualification or omitted references")
		}
		for _, ref := range view.Credentials {
			if ref.Role != "app" {
				value := f.reveal(ref)
				clear(value)
			}
		}
		first := f.await(f.deploy(view, "database_a").ID)
		a := f.inspect(first)
		volume := f.volumeProof(first)
		marker := "database_runner_" + engine + "_retained_marker"
		f.marker(view, first, marker, true)
		second := f.await(f.deploy(view, "database_b").ID)
		b := f.inspect(second)
		if f.volumeProof(second) != volume {
			t.Fatal("replacement recreated or relabeled volume")
		}
		if a.ID == b.ID || first.Plan.Storage.VolumeName != second.Plan.Storage.VolumeName || first.Plan.Database.NetworkName != second.Plan.Database.NetworkName || !reflect.DeepEqual(first.Plan.Database.Credentials, second.Plan.Database.Credentials) || a.NetworkSettings.Networks[first.Plan.Database.NetworkName].NetworkID != b.NetworkSettings.Networks[second.Plan.Database.NetworkName].NetworkID {
			t.Fatal("replacement changed retained storage/network/credentials or reused writer")
		}
		f.marker(view, second, marker, false)
		// Queue C with the runner stopped, then restart the compiled process using
		// the same protected roots. No database restart API is implied.
		f.stop()
		thirdID := f.deploy(view, "database_c").ID
		fault := &databaseRunnerFault{entered: make(chan struct{}), finished: make(chan struct{}), operationID: thirdID}
		if !f.fault.CompareAndSwap(nil, fault) {
			t.Fatal("completion fault already armed")
		}
		f.start()
		select {
		case <-fault.entered:
		case <-time.After(180 * time.Second):
			t.Fatal("real committed completion fault did not enter")
		}
		f.stop()
		select {
		case <-fault.finished:
		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
			t.Fatal("completion fault handler did not join")
		}
		third := f.await(thirdID)
		c := f.inspect(third)
		journal, err := runner.OpenAttemptJournal(filepath.Join(f.root, "journal"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal("stopped runner journal unavailable")
		}
		snapshot := journal.Snapshot()
		if journal.Close() != nil {
			t.Fatal("journal close failed")
		}
		pending := false
		for _, entry := range snapshot.Hosting {
			if entry.OperationID == thirdID && entry.Phase == "result" && entry.Database && entry.Result != nil && *entry.Result == fault.request {
				pending = true
			}
		}
		if !pending {
			t.Fatal("completion response loss did not retain exact durable result")
		}
		knownContainers := []domain.HostingOperation{first, second, third}
		beforeInventory := f.replayInventory(knownContainers, third)
		beforeComplete := f.completionCount(thirdID)
		beforeClaim := f.claimRequests.Load()
		beforeApply, beforeDelivery := f.applyRequests.Load(), f.deliveryRequests.Load()
		f.start()
		for deadline := time.Now().Add(30 * time.Second); ; {
			if f.completionCount(thirdID) > beforeComplete && f.claimRequests.Load() > beforeClaim {
				break
			}
			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
				t.Fatal("compiled restart did not replay completion")
			}
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
		}
		// Read-only public settled evidence and Docker identities must remain exact.
		replayed := f.await(thirdID)
		after := f.inspect(replayed)
		if f.volumeProof(replayed) != volume || after.NetworkSettings.Networks[third.Plan.Database.NetworkName].NetworkID != a.NetworkSettings.Networks[first.Plan.Database.NetworkName].NetworkID {
			t.Fatal("runner restart changed retained volume or private bridge")
		}
		if c.ID != after.ID || c.ID == b.ID || third.CompleteReceipt == nil || replayed.CompleteReceipt == nil || *third.CompleteReceipt != *replayed.CompleteReceipt || *third.Result != *replayed.Result || third.Plan.Storage.VolumeName != first.Plan.Storage.VolumeName || third.Plan.Database.NetworkName != first.Plan.Database.NetworkName || !reflect.DeepEqual(third.Plan.Database.Credentials, view.Credentials) {
			t.Fatal("completion replay duplicated writer or changed durable proof")
		}
		// Join the replay process before reopening its exclusive journal.
		f.stop()
		afterInventory := f.replayInventory(knownContainers, replayed)
		if databaseRunnerReplayInventoryMatches(beforeInventory, afterInventory, knownContainers, replayed) != nil {
			t.Fatal("Complete replay changed scoped all-state container or retained volume residue")
		}
		replayJournal, e := runner.OpenAttemptJournal(filepath.Join(f.root, "journal"))
		if e != nil {
			t.Fatal("replayed journal unavailable")
		}
		remaining := replayJournal.Snapshot()
		if replayJournal.Close() != nil {
			t.Fatal("replayed journal close failed")
		}
		for _, entry := range remaining.Hosting {
			if entry.OperationID == thirdID {
				t.Fatal("acknowledged database result remains pending")
			}
		}
		if f.completionCount(thirdID) != beforeComplete+1 || f.applyRequests.Load() != beforeApply || f.deliveryRequests.Load() != beforeDelivery {
			t.Fatal("completion replay refreshed credentials or repeated writer admission")
		}
		f.marker(view, replayed, marker, false)
		f.start()
		metadata := databaseRunnerJSON[domain.HostingDatabase](f, f.token, "GET", "/api/v1/resources/"+view.Resource.ID+"/database", nil, 200)
		if metadata.RuntimeState != domain.HostingDatabaseUnqualified || !reflect.DeepEqual(metadata.Credentials, view.Credentials) {
			t.Fatal("runtime fixture changed metadata contract")
		}
		t.Logf("engine=%s A=%s B=%s C=%s container=%s volume=%s network=%s recipe=%s child=%s", engine, first.ID, second.ID, third.ID, c.ID, third.Plan.Storage.VolumeName, third.Plan.Database.NetworkName, version, third.Release.CanonicalImage)
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerEnrollmentInputAcceptedByAPI(t *testing.T) {
	server, _ := newTestServer()
	token := createTestSession(t, server)
	post := func(path, bearer string, body any, status int) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
		t.Helper()
		raw, err := json.Marshal(body)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal("fixture enrollment input encoding failed")
		}
		defer clear(raw)
		r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, path, bytes.NewReader(raw))
		r.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+bearer)
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		server.ServeHTTP(rec, r)
		if rec.Code != status {
			t.Fatalf("fixture enrollment API path=%s status=%d want=%d", path, rec.Code, status)
		}
		return rec
	}
	caps := []string{domain.RunTypeDatabaseDeploy, domain.HostingDatabaseCapability, domain.HostingOwnedStorageCapability}

	var enrollment app.CreatedRunnerEnrollment
	if json.Unmarshal(created.Body.Bytes(), &enrollment) != nil {
		t.Fatal("fixture enrollment response decoding failed")
	}
	credential := "ncr_database_runner_fixture_only"
	consumed := post("/api/v1/runner-enrollments/consume", enrollment.Token, databaseRunnerEnrollmentConsumeInput(credential), http.StatusOK)
	var enrolled app.ConsumedRunnerEnrollment
	if json.Unmarshal(consumed.Body.Bytes(), &enrolled) != nil || enrolled.Runner.ID != "runner_database_acceptance" {
		t.Fatal("fixture enrollment returned a different runner")
	}
	post("/api/v1/runners/heartbeat", credential, struct{}{}, http.StatusOK)
	tlsServer := httptest.NewTLSServer(server)

	client.HTTP = tlsServer.Client()
	id, err := client.RuntimeExecutionIdentityWithOptions(t.Context(), runnerclient.RuntimeExecutionOptions{Database: true})
	if err != nil || id != enrolled.Runner.ID {
		t.Fatal("real API/client rejected the enrolled database runtime identity")
	}
	if _, err := client.RuntimeExecutionIdentityWithOptions(t.Context(), runnerclient.RuntimeExecutionOptions{}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("real API/client accepted database capabilities without configured database mode")
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerEarlyExitRetainsCleanupStatus(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, os.Args[0], "-test.run=^TestDatabaseRunnerExitChild$")
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "NEROCD_DATABASE_DIAGNOSTIC_EXIT_CHILD=1")
	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal("diagnostic child start failed")
	}
	p := newDatabaseRunnerProcess(cmd, cancel)
	f := &databaseRunnerFixture{t: t, process: p}
	t.Cleanup(f.stop)
	started := time.Now()
	op, reason := waitDatabaseRunnerOperation(ctx, p, func(context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
		return domain.HostingOperation{State: "dispatched"}, nil
	})
	if reason != "runner_exited" || (op.State != "" && op.State != "dispatched") || time.Since(started) > 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatal("database await did not promptly detect the exited runner")
	}
	want := databaseRunnerExit{Exited: true, Kind: "process_exit", Code: 7}
	first, second := p.status(), p.status()
	if first != want || second != want {
		t.Fatal("exit inspection consumed or changed retained status")
	}
	f.stop()
	f.stop()
	if f.process != nil || f.lastExit != want || p.status() != want || cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode() != 7 {
		t.Fatal("cleanup lost or changed the runner exit result")
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerExitCancelsInflightPoll(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	p := &databaseRunnerProcess{done: make(chan struct{})}
	blocked, published := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(published)
		select {
		case <-blocked:
			p.exit = databaseRunnerExit{Exited: true, Kind: "success", Code: 0}
			close(p.done)
		case <-ctx.Done():
		}
	}()
	defer func() { cancel(); <-published }()
	calls := 0
	started := time.Now()
	op, reason := waitDatabaseRunnerOperation(ctx, p, func(request context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
		calls++
		if calls == 1 {
			return domain.HostingOperation{State: "prepared", Plan: &domain.HostingApplyPlan{}}, nil
		}
		close(blocked)
		<-request.Done()
		return domain.HostingOperation{}, errors.New("secret poll error must not be rendered")
	})
	if reason != "runner_exited" || op.State != "prepared" || op.Plan == nil || time.Since(started) > 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatal("runner exit did not cancel the in-flight poll and retain the last operation")
	}
	if !p.status().Exited {
		t.Fatal("in-flight poll consumed runner exit evidence")
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerDiagnosticWhitelistRedaction(t *testing.T) {

	counts.record("GET", "/api/v1/hosting-operations/"+secret, 418)
	for range 10050 {

	}
	op := domain.HostingOperation{State: secret, ID: secret, RunID: secret, Snapshot: domain.HostingSnapshot{ImageReference: secret}, Plan: &domain.HostingApplyPlan{Hash: secret}, Result: &domain.HostingResult{Outcome: secret}, PreparedReceipt: &domain.HostingReceipt{ID: secret}}
	got := databaseRunnerDiagnostic(op, databaseRunnerExit{Exited: true, Kind: secret, Code: 1000}, &counts)
	want := "state=unknown release=false plan=true prepared=true result=true complete=false mutation_hold=false restore_hold=false runner_exited=true exit_kind=unknown exit_code=-1 api=[POST /api/v1/runners/claim 401=9999,GET /api/v1/hosting-operations/{id} 0=1]"
	if got != want || strings.Contains(got, secret) {
		t.Fatal("diagnostics escaped the fixed whitelist or count bound")
	}
	classified := databaseRunnerExitFor(errors.New(secret))
	if classified != (databaseRunnerExit{Exited: true, Kind: "wait_error", Code: -1}) {
		t.Fatal("runner error text escaped closed exit classification")
	}
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	w := &databaseRunnerStatusWriter{ResponseWriter: rec}
	if _, err := w.Write([]byte(secret)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal("status observer write failed")

		t.Fatal("status observer changed API response semantics")
	}
}

		return domain.HostingOperation{ID: id, BindingID: binding, ResourceID: resource, Plan: &domain.HostingApplyPlan{Hash: "plan_" + id, Storage: &domain.HostingStoragePlan{VolumeName: volume, MountPath: "/data"}}, Release: &domain.HostingRelease{Hash: "release_" + id, ImageID: "image_" + id}, Result: &domain.HostingResult{ContainerID: containerID}}

		var c databaseRunnerContainer
		c.ID = op.Result.ContainerID
		c.Image = op.Release.ImageID
		c.State.Running = running
		c.Config.Labels = map[string]string{"io.nerocd.binding": binding, "io.nerocd.operation": op.ID, "io.nerocd.plan": op.Plan.Hash, "io.nerocd.release": op.Release.Hash}
		c.Mounts = append(c.Mounts, struct {
			Type, Name, Source, Destination string
			RW                              bool
		}{Type: "volume", Name: volume, Destination: "/data", RW: true})
		return c
	}
	known := []domain.HostingOperation{previous, current}
	before := databaseRunnerReplayInventory{BindingContainers: []databaseRunnerContainer{container(current, true)}, VolumeUsers: []string{current.Result.ContainerID}}
	if err := databaseRunnerReplayInventoryMatches(before, before, known, current); err != nil {
		t.Fatal("unchanged scoped inventory rejected", err)
	}
	withStopped := databaseRunnerReplayInventory{BindingContainers: []databaseRunnerContainer{container(previous, false), container(current, true)}, VolumeUsers: []string{previous.Result.ContainerID, current.Result.ContainerID}}
	reordered := databaseRunnerReplayInventory{BindingContainers: []databaseRunnerContainer{container(current, true), container(previous, false)}, VolumeUsers: []string{current.Result.ContainerID, previous.Result.ContainerID}}
	if err := databaseRunnerReplayInventoryMatches(withStopped, reordered, known, current); err != nil {
		t.Fatal("unchanged known stopped identity rejected", err)
	}
	for _, change := range []string{"unknown_stopped_binding", "known_extra_stopped_binding", "foreign_stopped_volume_user", "lost_stopped_identity", "duplicate_binding", "foreign_label"} {
		t.Run(change, func(t *testing.T) {
			after := databaseRunnerReplayInventory{BindingContainers: slices.Clone(before.BindingContainers), VolumeUsers: slices.Clone(before.VolumeUsers)}
			start := before
			switch change {
			case "unknown_stopped_binding":
				extra := container(operation("unknown", strings.Repeat("c", 64)), false)
				after.BindingContainers = append(after.BindingContainers, extra)
				after.VolumeUsers = append(after.VolumeUsers, extra.ID)
			case "known_extra_stopped_binding":
				after.BindingContainers = append(after.BindingContainers, container(previous, false))
				after.VolumeUsers = append(after.VolumeUsers, previous.Result.ContainerID)
			case "foreign_stopped_volume_user":
				after.VolumeUsers = append(after.VolumeUsers, strings.Repeat("c", 64))
			case "lost_stopped_identity":
				start = databaseRunnerReplayInventory{BindingContainers: append(slices.Clone(before.BindingContainers), container(previous, false)), VolumeUsers: append(slices.Clone(before.VolumeUsers), previous.Result.ContainerID)}
			case "duplicate_binding":
				after.BindingContainers = append(after.BindingContainers, container(current, true))
			case "foreign_label":
				after.BindingContainers[0] = container(current, true)
				after.BindingContainers[0].Config.Labels["io.nerocd.binding"] = "foreign"
			}
			if databaseRunnerReplayInventoryMatches(start, after, known, current) == nil {
				t.Fatal("replay inventory accepted stopped or foreign residue")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerProtectedRevealDecoder(t *testing.T) {
	ref := domain.HostingDatabaseCredentialRef{Role: "app", Username: "ncd_app", SecretID: "fixture_secret", Version: 1}
	valid := fmt.Sprintf(`{"secret_id":"fixture_secret","version":1,"value":"%s"}`, strings.Repeat("A", 43))
	value, err := readDatabaseRunnerReveal(strings.NewReader(valid), ref)
	if err != nil || len(value) != 43 {
		t.Fatal("valid protected response rejected")
	}
	clear(value)
	for _, raw := range []string{valid + "{}", strings.Replace(valid, `"version":1`, `"version":2`, 1), strings.Replace(valid, `"version":1`, `"version":2,"version":1`, 1), strings.Replace(valid, `"value":`, `"Value":`, 1), strings.Replace(valid, "fixture_secret", "foreign", 1), strings.Replace(valid, `"value":`, `"extra":true,"value":`, 1), strings.Replace(valid, strings.Repeat("A", 43), "private diagnostic", 1), strings.Repeat("x", 8193)} {
		value, err := readDatabaseRunnerReveal(strings.NewReader(raw), ref)
		clear(value)
		if err == nil || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "private") {
			t.Fatal("protected decoder accepted or exposed invalid body")
		}
	}
}

func TestDatabaseRunnerFinalExitSamplePreservesFailureAndCurrentState(t *testing.T) {
	previous := domain.HostingOperation{State: "verifying", MutationHold: true}
	for _, state := range []string{"succeeded", "failed", "reconciliation_required", "verifying"} {
		t.Run(state, func(t *testing.T) {
			final := domain.HostingOperation{State: state, MutationHold: state == "reconciliation_required" || state == "verifying"}
			if state != "verifying" {
				final.Result = &domain.HostingResult{Outcome: "failed", Uncertain: state == "reconciliation_required"}
				final.CompleteReceipt = &domain.HostingReceipt{ID: "receipt"}
				if state == "succeeded" {
					final.Result.Outcome, final.Result.Ready = "succeeded", true
				}
			}
			reason := "runner_exited"
			calls := 0
			got, label := databaseRunnerFinalExitSample(t.Context(), previous, reason, func(ctx context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
				calls++
				deadline, ok := ctx.Deadline()
				if !ok || time.Until(deadline) > 2*time.Second || ctx.Err() != nil {
					t.Error("final read did not get a fresh bounded context")
				}
				return final, nil
			})
			if calls != 1 || label != "authoritative" || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, final) {
				t.Fatal("final diagnostic changed failure or lost current predicates")
			}
		})
	}
	calls := 0
	got, label := databaseRunnerFinalExitSample(t.Context(), previous, "runner_exited", func(context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
		calls++
		return domain.HostingOperation{}, errors.New("private_final_read_canary")
	})
	if calls != 1 || label != "stale" || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, previous) {
		t.Fatal("missing final sample asserted authority")
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
	cancel()
	got, label = databaseRunnerFinalExitSample(ctx, previous, "runner_exited", func(context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
		t.Fatal("canceled parent performed final read")
		return domain.HostingOperation{}, nil
	})
	if label != "stale" || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, previous) {
		t.Fatal("canceled diagnostic discarded retained evidence")
	}
	_, label = databaseRunnerFinalExitSample(t.Context(), previous, "deadline", func(context.Context) (domain.HostingOperation, error) {
		t.Fatal("non-exit performed final read")
		return domain.HostingOperation{}, nil
	})
	if label != "not_requested" {
		t.Fatal("ordinary wait failure was reinterpreted")
	}
}
```

```text
# Hosting compatibility ledger

Hosting-first documentation baseline: `65311f30470f34d0d26165d1cd13325fbd05fca0`.
Accepted application/source assessment:
`b7771468edf95f531c13d69b361ed901d9efbbc8`, 2026-10-24.
The Coolify reference remains
[`b12d1386f3d458618b4c579babcd1e339c6c40b3`](https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify/tree/b12d1386f3d458618b4c579babcd1e339c6c40b3).
Earlier planning at `a763a90b3896257b784c9498d01650ccdad2427a` and the
supplied revision 3 baseline `09d65d4ddcbfdf27e97158a9c08beb02a721818c`
are historical. Official documentation is separately dated and can change.

This ledger is the active delivery ledger: complete hosting R01–R68/A01–A37
and the declared matrices first. Direct hosting remains the primary navigation
and onboarding path; a Task or coding agent is not required.
The [workspace ledger](workspace-capabilities.md) separately covers Tasks,
Workspaces, machines, agents, models and shared results. The [plan](plan.md)
orders practical hosting, stateful hosting, remaining core parity and migration/
extended compatibility before the deferred D0–D3 workspace gates, preserving
all R01–R102 and A01–A66
in the [specification](product-spec.md). Feature, migration and unchanged-client
compatibility remain separate claims.

Any workspace-track work requires a [named hosting requirement, need now,
minimum scope and hosting acceptance test](plan.md#hosting-dependency-test).
Hosting contracts for remote builders, cache, releases, approvals and observations
can proceed without speculative workspace infrastructure. Trusted-host deployment
does not require a new VM backend; untrusted execution remains disabled until
its declared isolation requirements are satisfied.

## Status and evidence

- `planned`: required target without accepted implementation evidence.
- `partial`: bounded accepted foundations cover part of the capability.
- `implemented`: code exists without complete acceptance of the declared boundary.
- `validated`: named fixtures pass on a named candidate with stated limits.
- `intentionally different`: a declared behavior difference is supported explicitly.

Short fixture names in matrices are acceptance targets, not nonexistent tests
presented as passing. Real source paths below describe bounded evidence. Reports
retain their original revision; this documentation candidate runs no application
or runtime tests. No complete hosting parity or workspace milestone is inferred
by combining separate historical results.

### R42 remains an unfinished hosting workflow

The accepted internal prerequisites above passed integration checks and independent
code hygiene, specification and critical security reviews. They do not establish
application-to-database connectivity through the product. No connected R42 API/UI
workflow is accepted. Direct-engine alias qualification is bounded below.

The read-only origin observer, authenticated capture API/typed client, format 13
journal and private exact-ID capture coordinator are now accepted. Direct
private-engine origin capture and empty-v2 alias upgrades are physically
qualified at `d3849bb572ce5b7df40ef7324ef6bc71e8e08c92`.

The 27.89-second native Linux arm64 pass covers PostgreSQL 17.11 in 16.97 seconds
and Redis 8.2.10 in 10.92 seconds. A→B→C keeps the original volume, private
network and credential references. Separate authenticated clients resolve the
private hostname and read/write application records through replacements.
Reopened-engine observation checks host PID/UID 999 ownership and retained
origin bytes; a wrong actual alias is rejected. The
[fixture contract](../acceptance/runtime-hosting-database-origin-upgrade/README.md)
and [physical assertions](../internal/runnerruntime/hosting_database_origin_upgrade_runtime_integration_test.go)
define this bounded proof. Combined runtime/runner/client race checks, vet,
changed-code lint, Linux arm64 compilation and Go build also passed at that
revision. Local run evidence remains in
`/tmp/nerocd-database-origin-upgrade-20261024.ljtb01w9`.

Compiled capture/replay and normal database recovery are accepted at
`b7771468edf95f531c13d69b361ed901d9efbbc8`. The
[compiled-runner contract](../acceptance/runtime-hosting-database-runner/README.md)
and [capture/replay assertions](../internal/api/hosting_database_capture_runtime_integration_test.go)
cover real API/River source deployment, controller/materialization provenance
and the opt-in `--database-network-capture-id` path. Both PostgreSQL and Redis
passed without skips: capture/replay took 22.00 seconds and normal recovery
23.40 seconds. Evidence remains in
`/tmp/nerocd-database-runner-20261024.askzxzjj/runtime-test`.

Lost origin ACK retains the format 13 claim/plan/origin chain. Ordinary mode
holds; exact-ID historical replay succeeds with the owned socket absent and no
repeated claim, plan load, observation, credential delivery or Complete. Request
and historical ACK bytes, receipt identity and durable acknowledgment retirement
are preserved. Source, volume, network, credentials and protected state remain
unchanged. Normal A/B/C recovery preserves data and the exact completion receipt
after runner restart and lost completion ACK, without repeated writer admission.
The [completion regression](../internal/runnerruntime/hosting_database_completion_lifecycle_test.go)
checks authority-worker joining; the [UTC identity regression](../internal/store/postgres_hosting_database_network_capture_identity_test.go)
checks persisted JSON identity, with actual PostgreSQL source proof in 5.682 seconds.

This qualifies native Linux arm64/trusted Docker with a verified test CA.
Production ACME, untrusted workload isolation and broader host profiles remain
unqualified. The earlier direct alias-upgrade fixture retains its local
materialization limit; upgrade controller provenance is still unproved. Generic
capture dispatch, upgrade controller, application membership ledger/API/UI,
connected R42 binding, database-native backup/restore, rotation, full A17/A26/A37
and complete hosting parity remain unfinished.

## Database engines

The reference backup/restore distinctions below are retained from R44. PostgreSQL and Redis have bounded accepted hosting and direct origin/alias-upgrade evidence above; the other engines remain planned. Common container lifecycle code does not prove engine-specific backup, restore, credential rotation or major-version upgrade support.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | partial, bounded private hosting and direct alias upgrade accepted | Yes | Yes | PostgreSQL 17.11 API/compiled-runner recovery and capture/replay accepted at b777; direct origin/empty-v2 A→B→C proof retained at d384; connected R42 binding, rotation, engine-native backup and new-resource restore unfinished | db-postgresql-lifecycle, db-postgresql-restore, A17, A18, A26 |
| Redis | partial, bounded private hosting and direct alias upgrade accepted | No | No | Redis 8.2.10 API/compiled-runner recovery and capture/replay accepted at b777; direct origin/empty-v2 A→B→C persistence proof retained at d384; connected R42 binding, rotation and broader recovery unfinished | db-redis-lifecycle, db-redis-persistence |
| MySQL | planned, M3 | Yes | Yes | Engine-specific backup/import and application verification | db-mysql-backup-restore, db-mysql-upgrade |
| MariaDB | planned, M3 | Yes | Yes | Separate version/configuration tests from MySQL | db-mariadb-backup-restore, db-mariadb-upgrade |
| MongoDB | planned, M3 | Yes | Yes | Supported authentication and dump/import formats | db-mongodb-auth, db-mongodb-backup-restore |
| ClickHouse | planned, M3 | Yes | No | Backup parity; explicit restore procedure or labeled improvement | db-clickhouse-backup, db-clickhouse-restore-procedure |
| Dragonfly | planned, M3 | No | No | Hosting and persistence with explicit recovery limits | db-dragonfly-lifecycle, db-dragonfly-persistence |
| KeyDB | planned, M3 | No | No | Hosting and persistence with explicit recovery limits | db-keydb-lifecycle, db-keydb-persistence |
| SQLite | planned, experimental | Yes, experimental | Yes, experimental | Retain experimental label until versioned backup/restore fixtures pass | db-sqlite-experimental-backup-restore |

Every supported engine/version pair also needs readiness, credential rotation, network reachability, storage retention, incompatible-version rejection and application read/write evidence. No engine inherits these results from another row.

The [build-engine toolchain table](hosting-build-engine.md#host-and-toolchain-contract)
pins the accepted component and executable identities. The engine accepts one
Linux platform on its fixed native daemon; package receipts and the real fixture
cover that bounded local output. This does not claim a complete linux/amd64 and
linux/arm64 build-to-destination matrix or cross-host transfer. Each product
strategy still needs explicit architecture/version fixtures, credentials,
shared cache/retention controls and cross-host build-to-deploy evidence. Disk mode is
monitored with no finite overshoot guarantee, not a quota. Cancellation,
CPU/memory enforcement and expanded-output limits have bounded engine evidence
at the accepted build candidate cited above.

Compose compatibility includes managed and raw modes, service fields, interpolation required/default behavior, profiles, networks, volumes, operator labels, advanced host capabilities and versioned Docker Compose differential tests. Raw mode remains planned in P18; preflight rejects a protected policy if its release guarantees cannot be satisfied.

coverage using backend fixtures and the accepted combined Linux runtime and
browser gates. The managed image-to-routing path has isolated HTTP/trusted-HTTPS
coverage; this does not validate public DNS or production ACME. Same-host public source-build handoff and explicit managed route selection are accepted.
Continuous monitoring and additional certificate/proxy modes remain required.
A server's existing external proxy network does not prove managed routing
support, and the image-deployment UI's loopback HTTP result is not an HTTPS URL.

## Notification channels

Pinned source evidence is [Team notification configuration](https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify/blob/b12d1386f3d458618b4c579babcd1e339c6c40b3/app/Models/Team.php), C22.

| Channel | Status and slice | Supported limits | Planned fixtures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Email | planned, M2 | Configure credentials, event selection, bounded retry and actionable delivery result | notify-email, A25 |
| Generic webhook | planned, M2 | Scoped endpoint/credential, durable event identity, retry and duplicate handling | notify-webhook, A25 |
| Discord | planned, M3 | Separate channel adapter and delivery evidence | notify-discord |
| Slack | planned, M3 | Separate channel adapter and delivery evidence | notify-slack |
| Telegram | planned, M3 | Separate channel adapter and delivery evidence | notify-telegram |
| Pushover | planned, M3 | Separate channel adapter and delivery evidence | notify-pushover |

Each channel must redact credentials, preserve resource/project authorization, retain execution history and report partial outcomes. A successful database dump followed by failed upload must generate a useful notification while preserving local recovery data.

## Migration and client compatibility claims

Feature equivalence does not imply drop-in Coolify database or API compatibility. Native API/CLI/MCP support and Coolify client adapters have separate fixtures. Requested adapters require explicit endpoints, request/response/error contracts and version limits before a support claim.

NeroCD upgrades begin in M0 and preserve old IDs, approvals, effective permissions and in-flight execution semantics. Equal environment names are not an automatic grouping rule. Coolify import starts with read-only discovery and a versioned intermediate manifest. Missing secrets remain missing. A33 requires source automation suspension, final data synchronization, explicit traffic handoff, destination automation activation and a recovery policy for writes after cutover.

No full NeroCD domain migration, Coolify migration or unchanged-client
compatibility is validated at this assessment. Additive hosting and River
migration checks cover only their stated schema boundaries. Existing-container
adoption is a separate capability; discovered labels do not prove surrender of
the previous controller's authority.
```

```text
## Host and toolchain contract

The engine runs as an administrator on the Linux host of its fixed rootful Docker daemon. It requires cgroup v2, visibility of the daemon's storage and actual host process tree, an administrator-delegated cgroup directory, and support for OCI archive imports. The runtime fixture uses Docker 29.4.0 with its containerd image store. Classic Docker image stores are not a tested support target.

The rootful BuildKit container is privileged. The host, Docker daemon, Docker executable, Buildx executable, helper image, and administrative state directory are trusted. This boundary does not isolate hostile forks from the host. Build steps have no granted privileged entitlement, host network, host device, production credential, or workload Docker socket. BuildKit's own privileged daemon remains part of the trusted host.

`Config` is operator configuration. It never comes from a build request. `DockerBinary`, `BuildxBinary`, and `Socket` are fixed absolute paths. The engine supplies an empty Docker configuration, fixed Unix endpoint, and explicit process environment. It does not inherit Docker contexts, credential helpers, bearer tokens, SSH agents, registry passwords, or proxy variables.

The supported toolchain is pinned below. Image digests identify the published multi-architecture index. The runtime fixture selects the daemon's native Linux architecture.

| Component | Version | Immutable reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BuildKit | 0.34.1 | `moby/buildkit@sha256:99368f3e46177c6405b9740e4461d91cee004128daeecca78d4ceac50ec1da5c` |
| Dockerfile frontend | 1.28.0 | `docker/dockerfile@sha256:bb22d9815c728170f72750f4e5b0d672e06176142e1d602c7e66c050100b7e5b` |
| Railpack frontend | 0.40.1 | `ghcr.io/railwayapp/railpack-frontend@sha256:f1973377693af30c9b37a92c97c661c07b277ccdc6be909213c74c771f8d2d6d` |
| Static runtime | nginx 1.29.3 Alpine | `nginx@sha256:b3c656d55d7ad751196f21b7fd2e8d4da9cb430e32f646adcf92441b72f82b14` |
| Buildx Linux amd64 binary | 0.38.1 | `sha256:e25d5cd675092bb5d1d03632fdc46cdf3fede7b514dc5f023a105e00d3ce5ad4` |
| Buildx Linux arm64 binary | 0.38.1 | `sha256:3b83b3731916ba433feccaaa689fe5bcdc81c641d92c8e6c2ea865dfa141c97a` |
| Railpack amd64 musl archive | 0.40.1 | `sha256:2842de93e68713af9037e0bc0a398d7da78f3b96aa4804303a638db2bc69bd30` |
| Railpack arm64 musl archive | 0.40.1 | `sha256:c24a064b586b8f4f8c2fab44dd5ef19253e4c6cc4e1df793b3ae19cd87f7a5d4` |
| Mise amd64 musl archive | 2026.9.15 | `sha256:e331f3fa3c360c63e996ef70bc183ce178cb16d21f8bf4926c61cf6fa6b9fafd` |
| Mise arm64 musl archive | 2026.9.15 | `sha256:cf9a7c3e64688a7909fa69a4989d3b8daf6dd1b3e583fa0ab7c08139ae6d3dcd` |

Release asset checksums come from the official [Buildx release](https://github.com/docker/buildx/releases/tag/v0.38.1), [Railpack release](https://github.com/railwayapp/railpack/releases/tag/v0.40.1), and [Mise release](https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.9.15). BuildKit and Dockerfile references come from the official Docker registry. Railpack's custom frontend comes from its official GHCR repository. `gate.sh` verifies downloaded archive checksums before use. `New` checks the Buildx executable against the architecture's compiled-in checksum.

The pinned BuildKit image must already exist on the fixed daemon. `PlannerImage` is an immutable digest or local image ID of an operator-built helper. That helper contains the verified Railpack CLI at `/usr/local/bin/railpack` and Mise binary at `/usr/local/bin/mise`. The fixture builds this helper from verified archives. The engine does not download administrative executables.
```

Subject `563fb88f707b75563d03f0408df0267e3af473e9`. Reproduce with `git show 563fb88f707b75563d03f0408df0267e3af473e9:docs/postgres-operations.md` and select lines 1-180.

````text
# PostgreSQL Operations

NeroCD stores durable control-plane state in PostgreSQL when `NEROCD_DATABASE_URL`
is set. The in-memory store is for local development only.

## Migrations

Run migrations before starting a durable server:

```sh
NEROCD_DATABASE_URL=postgres://nerocd:nerocd_dev@127.0.0.1:5432/nerocd?sslmode=disable nerocd migrate --seed=false
```

The migrator records applied SQL files in `schema_migrations` with a checksum.
If an already-applied migration file changes, migration fails instead of
silently rewriting history.

## Backup

Use the bounded NeroCD wrapper for logical backups. It creates a new atomic
backup directory, writes a versioned manifest, records a SHA-256 checksum and
the applied migration ledger, and can inventory runner-file metadata without
copying any secret contents. The parent directory must already be owned by the
process running the command and have mode exactly `0700`.

```sh
mkdir -m 0700 /secure/nerocd-backups
nerocd backup --database-url "$NEROCD_DATABASE_URL" --output-dir /secure/nerocd-backups \
  --runner-file-root /secure/runner-files
```

The production profile has an opt-in, non-starting `tools` service, which runs
as UID 10001. For a host bind, provision the directory for that effective UID:

```sh
sudo install -d -m 0700 -o 10001 -g 10001 /secure/nerocd-backups
```

Rootless engines can map container UID 10001 to a different host UID. In that
case, create the bind directory with the engine's documented UID mapping, then
verify that `/backups` is owned by UID 10001 and mode `0700` inside the tools
container before backing up:

```sh
docker compose --env-file /secure/nerocd-production.env -f compose.production.yaml \
  --profile tools run --rm -T --entrypoint /bin/sh \
  -v /secure/nerocd-backups:/backups database-tools \
  -ec 'test "$(id -u)" = 10001; test "$(stat -c %u:%a /backups)" = 10001:700'
```

Do not change ownership of the operator-owned credential inputs. The tools
service receives only the migration-owner secret and no proxy network; never
mount the Docker socket.

```sh
docker compose --env-file /secure/nerocd-production.env -f compose.production.yaml \
  --profile tools run --rm -T \
  -v /secure/nerocd-backups:/backups \
database-tools backup --output-dir /backups
```

## Off-host Export and Verification

The local schedule is not disaster recovery by itself: its archive volume is
on the same host as PostgreSQL. Mount an operator-managed encrypted destination
(another machine, removable media, or a mounted backup service) and export a
completed archive. NeroCD does not require a cloud vendor or receive credentials
for that destination. It verifies the private manifest, exact dump checksum,
and archive shape before copying, then verifies the staged copy before atomically
publishing it with `0700` directory and `0600` file permissions.

```sh
mkdir -m 0700 /mnt/off-host/nerocd
nerocd backup-export \
  --input-dir /secure/nerocd-backups/backup-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ \
  --output-dir /mnt/off-host/nerocd
nerocd backup-verify \
  --input-dir /mnt/off-host/nerocd/export-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ
```

Perform this export after every scheduled backup and retain the exact NeroCD
image digest that created it. At least quarterly, create an isolated empty
PostgreSQL target on a different host, run `backup-verify`, then use `restore`
against that disposable target and confirm the restored schema ledger. Runner
file content is intentionally never copied; restore that material separately
from its own encrypted backup before performing the database restore.

## Local Backup Schedule

The production profile also contains a separate, non-root `backup-scheduler`
service. It is disabled by default: set `NEROCD_BACKUP_SCHEDULE_ENABLED=true`
only after provisioning the private `backup-data` volume and an approved local
collection procedure. The scheduler has only the migration-owner credential,
the internal database network, and that one owner-only volume; it cannot be
called through the API or browser.

It uses PostgreSQL time and a session advisory lock, so a restart continues the
stored next-run time and concurrent scheduler containers cannot overlap. A
missed interval causes at most one catch-up archive. Failed runs back off from
one minute up to the configured interval, with a durable cap of eight failures.
Successful runs retain only the configured number of newest canonical backup
directories; unsafe, unexpected, or symlinked archive content stops rotation
without deleting anything further. The manual `backup` and `restore` commands
remain unchanged and are still the procedure for an immediate operator action.

`/api/v1/operations/status` and protected `/metrics` expose only aggregate
schedule state (`disabled`, `waiting`, `due`, `running`, or `backoff`), time to
the next attempt, and the bounded failure count. They never expose archive
paths, database URLs, runner-file values, or tool diagnostics. Investigate a
`backoff` state by examining the private scheduler container logs, repairing
the local destination, and allowing the next DB-clock attempt; do not manually
delete unknown files from a backup directory.

## Restore

Restore only into a newly created, empty database. The command verifies the
manifest checksum and exact migration ledger before invalidating every active
session and runner lease; operators must issue fresh credentials and let the
reaper reconcile interrupted work. It never uses `--clean` against a live
target. Restore requires two explicit safeguards: `--allow-disposable-target`
and an exact `--confirm-target-database` name. Before `pg_restore`, NeroCD
holds a restore-admission advisory lock, rejects any other active DB session,
and rejects non-public schemas and objects in `public` or another user schema.
It does not terminate sessions for you.

```sh
createdb nerocd_restore
nerocd restore --database-url "$NEROCD_RESTORE_DATABASE_URL" \
  --input-dir /secure/nerocd-backups/backup-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ \
  --allow-disposable-target --confirm-target-database nerocd_restore \
  --runner-file-root /secure/runner-files
```

For production Compose, make a separate restore environment outside the
checkout. It needs a distinct project name, PostgreSQL password secret, owner
URL secret, app URL secret, owner role, app role, and proxy-network name. Set
the owner URL to the isolated project's `postgres` host and its `nerocd`
database; omit `NEROCD_DATABASE_URL` entirely. `compose.production.yaml`
hardcodes that database name, so confirming `nerocd` is safe only because this
is a separate cluster, network, and volumes.

`/secure/nerocd-restore.env` must explicitly set `NEROCD_IMAGE`,
`NEROCD_PROXY_NETWORK`, `NEROCD_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `NEROCD_OWNER_DATABASE_USER`,
`NEROCD_APP_DATABASE_USER`, `NEROCD_DATABASE_URL_SECRET`,
`NEROCD_APP_DATABASE_URL_SECRET`, and `NEROCD_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_SECRET` for
the restore project. It must name distinct restore secret files and roles, not
the production inputs. Source it in a subshell so values exported earlier from
the production environment cannot override Compose's restore inputs.

Start only the isolated PostgreSQL service and its required secret/data
initializers. Do not run `up` without a service name: that would run migration
or server services against the empty target.

```sh
(
  set -a; . /secure/nerocd-restore.env; set +a
  unset NEROCD_DATABASE_URL
  docker compose --project-name nerocd_restore_20260905 \
    --env-file /secure/nerocd-restore.env -f compose.production.yaml up -d postgres
  docker compose --project-name nerocd_restore_20260905 \
    --env-file /secure/nerocd-restore.env -f compose.production.yaml \
    --profile tools run --rm -T \
    -v /secure/nerocd-backups/backup-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ:/restore:ro \
    -v /secure/runner-files:/runner-files:ro \
  database-tools restore --input-dir /restore --runner-file-root /runner-files \
    --allow-disposable-target --confirm-target-database nerocd
)
```

The restore command itself rejects non-empty targets and other active database
sessions before `pg_restore`. After its checks and restore finish, stop and
remove this restore project; do not reuse its database for production.

## Runtime Checks

- `/api/v1/health` reports process liveness.
- `/api/v1/ready` checks that the configured store is reachable.
- `/metrics` exposes bounded-cardinality plain-text request counters and
  aggregate latency only to authenticated `system_admin` callers. In production
  it remains behind the approved proxy network; never publish it as a host port.
````

```text
//go:build linux && nerocd_proxy_fixture

package api
```
